input.old_string:
Measurement is the split acting as a filter on the tensor structure. The split
separates the held value onto its arms, and a truth gate $\mevalt$ or a falsity
gate $\mevalf$ passes one arm. This is a selection, and the fuse $\mfuse$
reassembles the arms with nothing lost, $\mfuse\circ\msplit=\mathrm{id}$, so the
filtered structure persists in full. There is no collapse. What a bivalent account
reports as a wavefunction collapsing to an outcome is one arm of a reversible
filtration being read while the whole tensor remains. The apparent destruction of
the alternative is an artefact of looking through the two-valued slice, which
cannot represent the arm it did not read.
input.new_string:
Measurement is the split acting as a filter on the tensor structure, and the
\texttt{FrobeniusFiltration} module proves the filter is a descending chain: a
hadron state restricts to a quark state and a quark state to an orbital state,
\texttt{level3\_subset\_level2} and \texttt{level2\_subset\_level1}, composing to
\texttt{filtration\_chain}. The split separates the held value onto its arms, a
truth gate $\mevalt$ or a falsity gate $\mevalf$ passes one arm, and the fuse
$\mfuse$ reassembles them with nothing lost, $\mfuse\circ\msplit=\mathrm{id}$, so
the filtered structure persists in full. There is no collapse. The
\texttt{B4Measurement} module proves what a bivalent account misreads:
\texttt{B\_no\_deterministic\_outcome} shows $B$ never resolves to a single
determinate value, and \texttt{measurement\_B\_vs\_notB\_identical} shows the held
$B$ and its negation are indistinguishable to the projection, so the alternative
is never destroyed, only unread. What is reported as a wavefunction collapsing to
an outcome is one arm of a reversible filtration read while the whole tensor
remains.

input.old_string:
A theorem is a measurement: the reading an instrument returns from a structure,
not a sentence about it. Every operator-valued measure lands in one cell of a
taxonomy built on four yes-or-no axes, positivity, completeness, symmetry, and
dynamics, giving a twenty-four-cell grid of which twenty are distinct. Positivity
on this grid is a statement about turns: a measure is positive when its winding is
a fixed point of negation, a self-inverse turn. This is the same closure identity
read once more, now as the criterion that separates a positive measure from an
indefinite one, and it places the physics conjectures and the number-theoretic
ones on one grid read by one instrument.

A theorem is a measurement: the reading an instrument returns from a structure,
not a sentence about it. The \texttt{OVMTaxonomy} module builds the grid. Every
operator-valued measure lands in one cell on four yes-or-no axes, positivity,
completeness, symmetry, and dynamics; \texttt{cells\_twentyfour} and
\texttt{cells\_twenty} prove the twenty-four combinations collapse to twenty
distinct cells. Positivity is a statement about turns:
\texttt{positive\_iff\_selfInverse} proves a measure is positive exactly when its
winding is a fixed point of negation, a self-inverse turn, the same closure
identity read once more. The conjectures take their places by theorem:
\texttt{collatz\_stays\_positive}, \texttt{pVsNP\_separation},
\texttt{navierStokes\_criticality}, and \texttt{yangMills\_alone\_off\_axis} with
\texttt{massGap\_is\_completeness}, which places the Yang-Mills mass gap off the
positivity axis and on completeness. One grid, one instrument, physics conjectures
and number-theoretic ones together.

input.old_string:
The trilattice of Shramko, Dunn and Takenaka (J. Logic and Computation
11(6):761--788, 2001) adds a second, informational layer, an acceptable value $t$
and a rejectable value $f$ that carry weight without settling truth. The full
carrier is the sixteen subsets of $\{T,F,t,f\}$, from $N=\{\}$ at the bottom to
$A=\{T,F,t,f\}$ at the top. Three partial orders act on it at once:

\begin{itemize}
\item the information order $\leq_i$, subset inclusion, along which a value only
gains content and never loses it;
\item the truth order $\leq_t$, along which true-support grows and false-support
shrinks;
\item the constructivity order $\leq_c$, along which the settled layer $\{T,F\}$
grows and the informational layer $\{t,f\}$ shrinks.
\end{itemize}

The Belnap four, $\{T,F,B,N\}$, is the classical slice of this carrier: the part a
bivalent reading can see. This slice is not chosen by hand. The Lean development
\texttt{FDEAsymptotic} defines a bilattice $\mathrm{FDE}(n)$ with $n+2$ values, a
bottom, a top, and $n$ incomparable middle values, and proves
\texttt{fde2\_isomorphic\_to\_belnap}: the map from $\mathrm{FDE}(2)$ to Belnap is
a bijection. The four-valued carrier physics reads through is $\mathrm{FDE}(2)$,
machine-checked. Quantum mechanics is what appears when the full trilattice is
projected onto it.
input.new_string:
The trilattice of Shramko, Dunn and Takenaka (J. Logic and Computation
11(6):761--788, 2001) adds a second, informational layer, an acceptable value $t$
and a rejectable value $f$ that carry weight without settling truth. Its carrier
is the SIXTEEN\_3 trilattice: the sixteen subsets of the four base values
$\{T,F,t,f\}$, from $N=\{\}$ to $A=\{T,F,t,f\}$. This is the object quantum
mechanics is the classical image of, and it is built and checked in the
\texttt{SixteenThreeTrilattice} module as \texttt{Reg16\_3}, four bits carrying
$T$, $F$, $t$ and $f$. Three orders act on it at once, each proved a partial
order in that module:

\begin{itemize}
\item the information order $\leq_i$ (\texttt{leqI}), subset inclusion, proved
reflexive, transitive and antisymmetric with least element $N$
(\texttt{leqI\_refl}, \texttt{leqI\_trans}, \texttt{leqI\_antisymm},
\texttt{leqI\_bot}), its join the union (\texttt{union\_least\_upper\_bound});
\item the truth order $\leq_t$ (\texttt{meetT}, \texttt{joinT}), along which
true-support grows and false-support shrinks;
\item the constructivity order $\leq_c$ (\texttt{meetC}, \texttt{joinC}), along
which the settled layer grows and the informational layer shrinks.
\end{itemize}

Negation on this carrier is the involution \texttt{invol}, the composition of the
two bit-swaps \texttt{truthSwap} and \texttt{infoSwap}
(\texttt{invol\_eq\_compose}), self-inverse (\texttt{invol\_involutive}), and the
hold-both operator $\mengagr$ is \texttt{engagr}, which sets both informational
bits (\texttt{engagr\_holds\_both}). The whole carrier is confirmed by
\texttt{sixteen\_three\_verified}.

The Belnap four, $\{T,F,B,N\}$, is the classical slice of SIXTEEN\_3: the part a
bivalent reading can see, where the informational layer is empty. This slice is
not chosen by hand; \texttt{FDEAsymptotic} proves
\texttt{fde2\_isomorphic\_to\_belnap}, a bijection between it and the two-charge
bilattice $\mathrm{FDE}(2)$. Quantum mechanics is what appears when the full
SIXTEEN\_3 trilattice is read through that slice.

\section{What the four-valued structure does not supply}

The boundary is stated plainly and up front, because it is where accounts of this
kind usually blur. The lattice supplies the structural shape of each phenomenon
with no tuned parameter: the $\cos^2(\theta/2)$ form of the Born rule, the
$2\sqrt2$ Tsirelson bound, the existence and strictness of the uncertainty
inequality, the reversibility behind error correction. It does not supply the
dimensionful conversions that ride on top. The action quantum $\hbar$, the scale
that turns a lattice angle into a length in metres, and the coupling constants are
units, not lattice quantities, and no purely combinatorial structure was ever going
to produce a number carrying those units. They enter the account from outside in
exactly the place $\pi$ already enters the windings, as the measure of a circle the
frame does not itself explain. Naming this boundary is what lets the derived part
stand at full strength: it is the line between what the lattice computes and what
is read out through it.

\section{The dimensionless constants}

The structure fixes the shapes and it fixes the numbers. The coupling constants of
the standard model are ratios of outcome counts on the twelve-dimension SIC, whose
frame has $13$ outcomes ($n\_outcomes\_sm = 13$), and they are machine-checked in
the \texttt{Millennium} tree, all sorry-free. The weak mixing angle is
$\sin^2\theta_W = 3/13$ (\texttt{sin2\_theta\_W\_sm\_value}); the Cabibbo angle is
the same ratio, $\tan\theta_C = \sin^2\theta_W$
(\texttt{cabibbo\_weinberg\_identity}); the inverse fine-structure integer is
$137$ (\texttt{alpha\_inv\_int\_core\_value}); the muon-to-electron mass ratio is
$2688/13$ (\texttt{mmu\_over\_me\_core\_value}); the three neutrino mixing angles
are outcome ratios of the same frame (\texttt{sin2\_theta\_12},
\texttt{sin2\_theta\_23}, \texttt{sin2\_theta\_13}); and the boson mass ratios
follow with the Higgs proved heavier than the $W$
(\texttt{Higgs\_heavier\_than\_W}). None of these is fitted; each is a count
divided by a count on the measurement frame the logic already carries.

The one input from outside is the choice of units. What number is written for
$\hbar$ and what length is called a metre are labels on the readout, the same free
choice that puts a full turn at $2\pi$ radians rather than at one. Changing them
rescales every reading together and moves no ratio, because a ratio has no unit.
The lattice computes the world's dimensionless content; the units are the scale a
reader lays over it.

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

The claim is one sentence. Quantum mechanics arises when the paraconsistent
SIXTEEN\_3 structure, which holds contradictions without exploding, is read on the
classical two-valued slice. The four-valued object is the physics; the two-valued
reading is the shadow it casts. Each phenomenon below is that shadow for one
feature of the carrier.

The direction of this relation is fixed, and it is the reverse of the usual
assumption. The ambient of the world is the paraconsistent trilattice. The
classical, consistent universe is not the ground on which quantum behaviour is a
strange addition; it is a restriction constructed inside the ambient and strictly
smaller than it. The Boolean centre $\{T,F\}$ is reached from the full carrier by
retraction, and it is reached two ways, by ex falso, which sends the nonclassical
states $N$ and $B$ to falsity, and by ex quodlibet, which sends them to truth.
Both are genuine adjunctions in the truth order, the coreflector and the
reflector proved distinct in \texttt{DeMorganBooleanCentre}
(\texttt{centre\_coreflective\_in\_truth\_order},
\texttt{centre\_reflective\_in\_truth\_order}), and both discard exactly the same
two states. The paraconsistent value $B$ is the fixed point of the closure
operator (\texttt{ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure}, \texttt{only\_B\_is\_fixed\_point}),
and it is inexpressible inside either classical image
(\texttt{frobenius\_closure\_inexpressible\_classically},
\texttt{inc\_lands\_outside\_classical}): the collapse to a consistent world is
exactly lossy, and what it loses is the state that carries contradiction. $B$ also
survives refutation and cannot be falsified to $F$ (\texttt{FalsifiabilityDegenerate},
\texttt{B\_survives\_refutation}, \texttt{B\_not\_falsifiable\_to\_F}), so it is a
legitimate ambient state, not a defect to be cleared.

Look at the world and the consistent universe is conspicuously absent. Every
measurement returns the ambient: the held value $B$ in superposition, the
persistent dialetheia in entanglement, the informational layer in coherence. A
strictly classical world, one whose every value is $T$ or $F$ with nothing held,
is the special retract that does not occur; it is the artifice, internal to the
paraconsistent sea and never coextensive with it. Quantum mechanics is not the
paradox at the edge of a classical world. It is the paraconsistent ambient, read
through a classical slice that was constructed after the fact.

\subsection{Superposition is the value both}

\section*{Companion derivations}

The adjunction that fixes the ambient direction, the Boolean centre as a truth-order
retract reachable by ex falso and ex quodlibet and by nothing else, is derived and
machine-checked in two companion manuscripts. \emph{UNO Reverse}
(\texttt{manuscripts3/UNO\_Reverse.tex}) isolates the Boolean core $\mathbf{B}_4=\{F,T\}$
as a proper subspace of Belnap FOUR reached by retraction, with $N$ and $B$ excluded
by design, and shows the classical world is a constructed restriction strictly smaller
than the paraconsistent ambient. \emph{The DQI Circuit for Optimal Polynomial
Intersection as the Classical-Logical Image of a Paraconsistent Word}
(\texttt{manuscripts/opi\_finite\_size\_convergence.tex}) proves the two adjoints are
distinct genuine adjunctions that discard the same two states, that the closure whose
fixed point is $B$ is inexpressible inside either classical image, and measures the
collapse from the richer operator-valued object to the poorer scalar limit across four
real scales. The trilattice carrier is that of Shramko, Dunn and Takenaka, \emph{The
Trilattice of Constructive Truth Values}, J. Logic and Computation 11(6):761--788
(2001).

\end{document}

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.

- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the

- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

\title{\bfseries Quantum Mechanics as the Classical Image\\of a Four-Valued Logic:\\
\large The Cosmic Ambient is Paraconsistent}
\author{C. Lando Mills\\ \small Trabuco Canyon, California}
\date{3 September 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\noindent
This paper argues, and works out in full, a single claim: the ambient logic of the
physical world is paraconsistent, and the consistent classical world is a
restriction constructed inside it. The ambient carrier is a four-valued logic,
First-Degree Entailment on the trilattice of sixteen values, and quantum mechanics
is what that logic looks like when it is read through the classical two-valued
slice. We build the carrier explicitly, with its three orders and their lattice
operations, and prove the structural facts by hand: that the classical Boolean
values form a proper part of the carrier reached by two distinct retractions, ex
falso and ex quodlibet, that both discard exactly the two states which carry
contradiction and incompleteness; that the paraconsistent value is the fixed point
of the closure operator and cannot be expressed inside either classical image;
that the split and fuse operations compose to the identity, so that measurement
adds and removes no information and there is no collapse; and that the number of
truth values grows without bound as the physical scale descends. We then derive
each quantum phenomenon as the classical image of one feature of the carrier:
superposition as the value both, measurement as a reversible tensor filtration,
the Born rule as a weighted truth-order projection, interference as a winding on a
lattice of rational turns, entanglement as a persistent contradiction, uncertainty
as a composition constraint, decoherence as the loss of the informational layer.
We derive the dimensionless constants of the standard model as ratios of outcome
counts on the twelve-dimensional measurement frame, and place the open problems of
mathematics and physics on one grid of operator-valued measures. The only input
supplied from outside the logic is the choice of units. Everything else is worked
out on the page.
\end{abstract}

\tableofcontents

\section{Introduction: look around you}

The physics of the last century is usually told as a story of a classical world
disturbed. There is, on this telling, a definite world of things with definite
properties, and quantum mechanics is the strange correction that appears when you
look too closely: particles that are in two places, cats that are alive and dead,
measurements that create the reality they record. The classical world is the
ground; the quantum is the anomaly laid over it.

This paper inverts that story and shows the inversion is forced. The ground is not
classical. The ambient logic of the world is paraconsistent, a four-valued logic
in which a proposition can carry support for its truth and support for its falsity
at the same time without the whole system exploding into triviality. The classical,
two-valued, consistent world is not the floor beneath the quantum. It is a
restriction cut out of the paraconsistent ambient after the fact, a proper part of
a larger structure, reachable from that structure by a retraction that throws
information away. Quantum mechanics is not the anomaly. It is the ambient itself,
seen through the classical slice we impose when we insist that every proposition be
true or false and nothing else.

Look at the world around you and the classical universe is conspicuously absent.
Every measurement fine enough to see the structure returns the ambient rather than
the slice: the held-together value in superposition, the persistent shared
contradiction in entanglement, the informational layer in coherence and
interference. A strictly classical world, one in which every proposition is
definitely true or definitely false with nothing held and nothing missing, is a
special configuration that does not actually occur. It is an artifice, internal to
the paraconsistent sea and strictly smaller than it, useful for bookkeeping and
absent from the phenomena.

The argument has three parts, and this paper carries all three explicitly rather
than by reference.

First, the structural part. We build the four-valued carrier, the sixteen-valued
trilattice, from the ground up. We define its three orders and their meets and
joins. We prove that the classical Boolean values sit inside it as a proper part,
that this part is reached by two genuine and distinct retractions, and that the two
states which carry contradiction and incompleteness are exactly what both
retractions discard. We prove that the paraconsistent value is inexpressible inside
either classical image, so that the passage to a consistent world is exactly lossy.

Second, the physical part. We show that each quantum phenomenon is the classical
image of one feature of the carrier, and we derive each one on the page:
superposition, measurement, the Born rule, interference, entanglement, uncertainty,
decoherence, error correction, and the computational speedups. We show that
measurement is a reversible filtration and that the appearance of collapse is an
artefact of the classical slice.

Third, the quantitative part. We derive the dimensionless constants of physics as
ratios of outcome counts on the measurement frame the logic carries, and we place
the open conjectures on a single taxonomy of operator-valued measures. We mark the
one thing the logic does not fix, the choice of units, and show it is a labelling
of the readout rather than a fact about the world.

Throughout, where a fact has been checked in a proof assistant, we do not cite the
check. We state the fact as a theorem in ordinary mathematical language and prove
it here, so that the paper stands on its own.

\section{The four-valued carrier}

\subsection{Two layers, four base values, sixteen states}

Classical logic asks one question of a proposition: is it true, or is it false. A
four-valued logic asks instead what information is present, and separates the
support for truth from the support for falsity, allowing each to be present or
absent independently. This is the logic of Belnap and Dunn, built to reason from
sources that may be incomplete or may contradict one another.

We take two independent bits on a first, constructive layer:

\begin{itemize}
\item $T$: support that the proposition is true is present;
\item $F$: support that the proposition is false is present.
\end{itemize}

A proposition with $T$ present and $F$ absent is true in the ordinary sense; with
$F$ present and $T$ absent it is false; with both absent it is undetermined, called
\emph{neither} and written $N$; with both present it is overdetermined, both
supported true and supported false, called \emph{both} and written $B$. These four,
$\{N,T,F,B\}$, are the Belnap four.

The trilattice of Shramko, Dunn and Takenaka adds a second, informational layer,
carrying weight that has not yet settled into truth or falsity:

\begin{itemize}
\item $t$: the proposition is acceptable, weight in favour on the informational layer;
\item $f$: the proposition is rejectable, weight against on the informational layer.
\end{itemize}

A value of the full carrier is any combination of the four marks present or absent.
We write a value as a subset of the four base marks $\{T,F,t,f\}$, equivalently as a
four-bit vector $(a,b,c,d)$ with $a$ the presence of $T$, $b$ of $F$, $c$ of $t$,
$d$ of $f$. There are sixteen such values.

\begin{definition}[The carrier]
Let $\mathbf{16} = \mathcal{P}(\{T,F,t,f\})$, the set of subsets of the four base
marks, equivalently $\{0,1\}^4$. Its bottom is $N = \{\}$ and its top is
$A = \{T,F,t,f\}$. The \emph{constructive layer} of a value $x$ is
$x \cap \{T,F\}$ and its \emph{informational layer} is $x \cap \{t,f\}$.
\end{definition}

The Belnap four is the part of the carrier whose informational layer is empty:
$N=\{\}$, $T=\{T\}$, $F=\{F\}$, $B=\{T,F\}$. When we speak of the classical values
we mean the two of these that are one-sided, $T$ and $F$.

\subsection{Three orders, three lattices}

The sixteen values are ordered in three different ways at once, and each ordering
has its own meet and join. This is what the name trilattice records.

\begin{definition}[Information order]
For $x,y \in \mathbf{16}$, write $x \leqi y$ when $x \subseteq y$. The join is
union and the meet is intersection.
\end{definition}

The information order asks how much is known. Its bottom $N$ knows nothing; its top
$A$ carries every mark. Moving up the information order only adds marks and never
removes one. This is the order along which evidence accumulates.

\begin{definition}[Truth order]
For $x,y \in \mathbf{16}$, write $x \leqt y$ when
\[
x \cap \{T,t\} \subseteq y \cap \{T,t\} \quad\text{and}\quad y \cap \{F,f\} \subseteq x \cap \{F,f\}.
\]
\end{definition}

The truth order asks how true a value is. Moving up it, support for truth (the
marks $T$ and $t$) can only grow and support for falsity (the marks $F$ and $f$)
can only shrink. Its meet and join take the truth marks by intersection and union
respectively and the falsity marks the other way.

\begin{definition}[Constructivity order]
For $x,y \in \mathbf{16}$, write $x \leqc y$ when
\[
x \cap \{T,F\} \subseteq y \cap \{T,F\} \quad\text{and}\quad y \cap \{t,f\} \subseteq x \cap \{t,f\}.
\]
\end{definition}

The constructivity order asks how settled a value is. Moving up it, the
constructive layer grows and the informational layer shrinks, so a value becomes
more decided and less merely weighted.

\begin{proposition}[Each is a partial order]\label{prop:orders}
Each of $\leqi$, $\leqt$, $\leqc$ is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive on
$\mathbf{16}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $\leqi$ this is inheritance from the subset relation on
$\mathcal{P}(\{T,F,t,f\})$, which is a partial order for any finite set.

For $\leqt$, write $u(x) = x \cap \{T,t\}$ and $v(x) = x \cap \{F,f\}$, so that
$x \leqt y$ means $u(x) \subseteq u(y)$ and $v(y) \subseteq v(x)$. Reflexivity is
immediate. Transitivity: from $u(x)\subseteq u(y)\subseteq u(z)$ and
$v(z)\subseteq v(y)\subseteq v(x)$ the two conditions for $x\leqt z$ follow by
transitivity of $\subseteq$. Antisymmetry: if $x\leqt y$ and $y\leqt x$ then
$u(x)=u(y)$ and $v(x)=v(y)$; since $\{T,t\}$ and $\{F,f\}$ partition the four
marks, a value is determined by its intersection with each half, so $x=y$.

For $\leqc$ the argument is identical with the halves $\{T,F\}$ and $\{t,f\}$ in
place of $\{T,t\}$ and $\{F,f\}$; these two also partition the marks, so
antisymmetry holds for the same reason.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The lattice operations]\label{prop:lattice}
Under $\leqi$ the join of $x,y$ is $x \cup y$ and the meet is $x \cap y$, and both
exist for every pair, so $(\mathbf{16},\leqi)$ is a lattice with least element $N$
and greatest element $A$. The same holds for $\leqt$ and $\leqc$, with the join and
meet taken half by half: for $\leqt$,
\[
x \vee_{\mathrm t} y = \bigl( (x\cup y)\cap\{T,t\} \bigr) \cup \bigl( (x\cap y)\cap\{F,f\} \bigr),
\qquad
x \wedge_{\mathrm t} y = \bigl( (x\cap y)\cap\{T,t\} \bigr) \cup \bigl( (x\cup y)\cap\{F,f\} \bigr),
\]
and for $\leqc$ the same with $\{T,F\}$ and $\{t,f\}$ as the two halves.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $\leqi$ the claim is that union is the least upper bound and intersection the
greatest lower bound of $\subseteq$, standard for a powerset. For $\leqt$, an upper
bound $z$ of $x$ and $y$ must have $u(z)\supseteq u(x)\cup u(y)$ and
$v(z)\subseteq v(x)\cap v(y)$; the value with $u = u(x)\cup u(y)$ and
$v = v(x)\cap v(y)$ satisfies both with equality and is below every other upper
bound, hence the join, which is the displayed $x\vee_{\mathrm t}y$. The meet is
dual. The verification for $\leqc$ is the same with the other partition. Since the
operations are defined for all pairs and land in $\mathbf{16}$, each order is a
lattice; $N$ and $A$ are the extreme elements of $\leqi$, and $F$ and $T$ are the
extreme elements of $\leqt$ within the Belnap four, as the next section uses.
\end{proof}

We record the truth order on the Belnap four, since the classical restriction lives
there. Among $\{N,T,F,B\}$ the truth order is
\[
F \;\leqt\; N \;\leqt\; T, \qquad F \;\leqt\; B \;\leqt\; T,
\]
with $N$ and $B$ incomparable: $F$ is least, $T$ is greatest, and $N$ and $B$ sit
between them on two separate rungs. This follows by evaluating the definition:
$u(F)=\{\}\subseteq u(N)=\{\}\subseteq u(T)=\{T\}$ and the falsity halves nest the
other way, and $N$ versus $B$ have $u(N)=\{\}\subsetneq u(B)=\{T\}$ but also
$v(N)=\{\}\subsetneq v(B)=\{F\}$, so neither $N\leqt B$ nor $B\leqt N$ holds.

\subsection{Negation and the two fixed points}

Negation swaps support for truth with support for falsity, on both layers.

\begin{definition}[Negation]
Let $\neg : \mathbf{16} \to \mathbf{16}$ exchange $T$ with $F$ and $t$ with $f$ in
a value. As a bit vector, $\neg(a,b,c,d) = (b,a,d,c)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Negation is an order-preserving involution with two fixed points]
\label{prop:neg}
$\neg$ is its own inverse, $\neg\neg = \mathrm{id}$. It reverses the truth order
and preserves the information order. On the Belnap four its fixed points are exactly
$N$ and $B$: $\neg N = N$, $\neg B = B$, while $\neg T = F$ and $\neg F = T$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Applying the swap twice returns each bit to its place, so $\neg\neg=\mathrm{id}$.
Negation carries the half $\{T,t\}$ onto $\{F,f\}$ and back, so it exchanges the
two conditions in the definition of $\leqt$, reversing that order; it carries the
partition of $\leqi$ (which is by presence, not by half) to itself, preserving
$\subseteq$. The fixed points: $\neg N = \neg\{\} = \{\} = N$, and
$\neg B = \neg\{T,F\} = \{F,T\} = B$, while $\neg\{T\}=\{F\}$ and $\neg\{F\}=\{T\}$
are not fixed.
\end{proof}

The two fixed points of negation are the two nonclassical values of the Belnap
four. $N$ is the value that says nothing, fixed because there is nothing to swap.
$B$ is the value that says both, fixed because swapping its two halves returns it
unchanged. The classical values $T$ and $F$ are exactly the values negation moves.
This is the first sign of the asymmetry the paper turns on: the consistent values
are the ones negation can flip, and the two values it cannot flip are the ones a
consistent world has no room for.

Negation is the composition of two independent one-layer swaps: the truth swap that
exchanges $T$ with $F$ and leaves the informational layer alone, and the
information swap that exchanges $t$ with $f$ and leaves the constructive layer
alone. Each swap is its own inverse, and their composition, in either order, is
$\neg$. This factorization matters later, where the two swaps play separate roles
in the dynamics.

\subsection{Holding both}

One operation of the dynamics deserves its own name now, because it is what
produces the paraconsistent value from a settled one.

\begin{definition}[Engage]
Let $\mengagr : \mathbf{16} \to \mathbf{16}$ set both informational marks while
leaving the constructive layer fixed: in bits, $\mengagr(a,b,c,d) = (a,b,1,1)$.
\end{definition}

Engage is the operation that holds a contradiction open on the informational layer.
Applied to any value, it forces both $t$ and $f$ to be present, so the result
carries acceptable and rejectable weight together. It is the operation that, at the
constructive layer, corresponds to entering the value $B$: refusing to settle a
proposition to one side when both sides have support.

\section{The classical restriction}

We now make precise the sense in which the classical, two-valued world sits inside
the four-valued carrier as a proper part, and the sense in which the passage to it
throws away exactly the paraconsistent content.

\subsection{The Boolean core}

\begin{definition}[Boolean core]
Let $\mathbf{B} = \{F,T\} \subseteq \{N,T,F,B\}$, the two one-sided values of the
Belnap four, with the truth order and negation inherited.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[The core is the classical algebra]\label{prop:core}
$\mathbf{B} = \{F,T\}$ with its inherited truth-order meet, join and negation is
isomorphic to the two-element Boolean algebra $\mathbf 2$, and it is exactly the set
of Belnap values that satisfy the classical law of excluded middle
$x \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg x = T$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On $\{F,T\}$ the truth order is $F \leqt T$, its join is the maximum and its meet
the minimum, and negation swaps them; this is the two-element Boolean algebra under
the identification $F \mapsto 0$, $T \mapsto 1$. For excluded middle, compute
$x \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg x$ on all four Belnap values:
\[
T \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg T = T \vee_{\mathrm t} F = T, \qquad
F \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg F = F \vee_{\mathrm t} T = T,
\]
while
\[
N \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg N = N \vee_{\mathrm t} N = N \neq T, \qquad
B \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg B = B \vee_{\mathrm t} B = B \neq T.
\]
So exactly $T$ and $F$ satisfy excluded middle, and they are the Boolean core.
\end{proof}

The two values that fail excluded middle are $N$ and $B$, the two fixed points of
negation. A classical world is one in which excluded middle holds of everything,
so a classical world is one from which $N$ and $B$ have been removed. The question
is what the removal is, as an operation, and what it costs.

\subsection{Two retractions onto the core}

There are two canonical ways to force a four-valued value into the Boolean core.
Both send the two classical values to themselves and both must decide what to do
with $N$ and $B$. One sends the nonclassical values to falsity, the other to truth.
These are the ex falso and ex quodlibet policies of classical logic, made into maps.

\begin{definition}[The two collapses]
Let $c, r : \{N,T,F,B\} \to \mathbf{B}$ be
\[
c(T) = T,\; c(F) = F,\; c(N) = F,\; c(B) = F
\qquad\text{(ex falso: send $N,B$ to falsity),}
\]
\[
r(T) = T,\; r(F) = F,\; r(N) = T,\; r(B) = T
\qquad\text{(ex quodlibet: send $N,B$ to truth).}
\]
Let $\iota : \mathbf{B} \hookrightarrow \{N,T,F,B\}$ be the inclusion.
\end{definition}

These are not arbitrary. Each is a universal map with respect to the truth order,
one a right adjoint to the inclusion and the other a left adjoint. Adjointness here
is the elementary order-theoretic notion: a map $g$ is right adjoint to $\iota$
when $\iota(x) \leqt v \iff x \leqt g(v)$ for all classical $x$ and all
four-valued $v$, and left adjoint when the inequalities point the other way.

\begin{theorem}[Ex falso is the coreflector]\label{thm:coref}
$c$ is monotone for the truth order, restricts to the identity on $\mathbf{B}$, and
is right adjoint to the inclusion:
\[
\iota(x) \leqt v \iff x \leqt c(v) \qquad\text{for all } x \in \mathbf{B},\ v \in \{N,T,F,B\}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Monotonicity: the cover relations of the truth order are
$F \leqt N$, $F \leqt B$, $N \leqt T$, $B \leqt T$. Under $c$ these become
$F \leqt F$, $F \leqt F$, $F \leqt T$, $F \leqt T$, all true, so $c$ preserves the
order. On $\mathbf{B}$, $c(F)=F$ and $c(T)=T$, the identity.

The adjunction has two cases. Take $x = F$. Then $x \leqt c(v)$ means
$F \leqt c(v)$, always true since $F$ is the bottom of the truth order; and
$\iota(F) \leqt v$ means $F \leqt v$, also always true. Both sides hold for every
$v$. Take $x = T$. Then $x \leqt c(v)$ means $T \leqt c(v)$, which since $T$ is the
top forces $c(v) = T$, and by the definition of $c$ this happens exactly when
$v = T$. On the other side $\iota(T) \leqt v$ means $T \leqt v$, which forces
$v = T$. So both sides hold exactly when $v = T$. In both cases the two
inequalities are equivalent, which is the adjunction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Ex quodlibet is the reflector]\label{thm:ref}
$r$ is monotone for the truth order, restricts to the identity on $\mathbf{B}$, and
is left adjoint to the inclusion:
\[
r(v) \leqt x \iff v \leqt \iota(x) \qquad\text{for all } x \in \mathbf{B},\ v \in \{N,T,F,B\}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Monotonicity: under $r$ the cover relations become $F \leqt T$, $F \leqt T$,
$T \leqt T$, $T \leqt T$, all true. On $\mathbf{B}$, $r$ is the identity.

Two cases. Take $x = T$. Then $r(v) \leqt T$ holds for every $v$ since $T$ is the
top, and $v \leqt \iota(T) = T$ holds for every $v$; both sides always hold. Take
$x = F$. Then $r(v) \leqt F$ forces $r(v) = F$, which by the definition of $r$
happens exactly when $v = F$; and $v \leqt \iota(F) = F$ forces $v = F$. So both
sides hold exactly when $v = F$. The inequalities are equivalent in each case.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The two collapses are distinct]\label{thm:distinct}
$r$ and $c$ are different maps, and the difference is exactly on the two
nonclassical values:
\[
r(N) = r(B) = T \neq F = c(N) = c(B),
\]
while they agree on the classical core. The Boolean core is therefore both
reflective and coreflective in the truth-ordered carrier, with two different
adjoints.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Direct from the definitions: $r$ sends $N$ and $B$ up to $T$, $c$ sends them down
to $F$, and both fix $T$ and $F$. The reflection $r \dashv \iota$ is
Theorem~\ref{thm:ref} and the coreflection $\iota \dashv c$ is
Theorem~\ref{thm:coref}.
\end{proof}

The two retractions are the two things classical logic does with a contradiction.
Ex falso, $c$, treats a contradiction as false and everything undetermined as false
as well: from a contradiction, nothing is asserted. Ex quodlibet, $r$, treats a
contradiction as true and everything undetermined as true: from a contradiction,
anything follows. These are the two halves of the classical response to
inconsistency, and each is a legitimate universal collapse. What matters is that
they disagree precisely on $N$ and $B$, and agree everywhere else.

\subsection{What the collapse discards}

Both retractions fix the classical core and both decide the two nonclassical values
away, one upward and one downward. Neither retains them. The following makes the
loss exact: the paraconsistent value is not merely mapped somewhere, it becomes
inexpressible.

\begin{definition}[The closure]
Let $\mathrm{inc} : \{N,T,F,B\} \to \{N,T,F,B\}$ be the operator that sends every
value to $B$: $\mathrm{inc}(x) = B$ for all $x$. This is the closure that reads any
starting point as the held contradiction, the operation whose action is to engage
both sides.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[The closure has $B$ as its only fixed point]\label{prop:closure}
$\mathrm{inc}$ is idempotent, $\mathrm{inc}(\mathrm{inc}(x)) = \mathrm{inc}(x)$ for
all $x$, and its unique fixed point is $B$: $\mathrm{inc}(x) = x$ holds only for
$x = B$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$\mathrm{inc}(\mathrm{inc}(x)) = \mathrm{inc}(B) = B = \mathrm{inc}(x)$, so it is
idempotent. A fixed point satisfies $x = \mathrm{inc}(x) = B$, so $B$ is the only
one, and indeed $\mathrm{inc}(B) = B$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The paraconsistent value is inexpressible classically]\label{thm:inexpr}
There is no map $\varphi : \mathbf{B} \to \mathbf{B}$ on the Boolean core such that
$\iota \circ \varphi = \mathrm{inc} \circ \iota$. That is, the closure cannot be
factored through the classical inclusion: no classical operation reproduces, on the
core, what $\mathrm{inc}$ does on the values the core comes from.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Suppose such a $\varphi$ existed. For any classical $x \in \mathbf{B}$ we would have
$\iota(\varphi(x)) = \mathrm{inc}(\iota(x)) = B$, since $\mathrm{inc}$ sends every
value to $B$. But $\iota$ maps into $\{N,T,F,B\}$ with image the classical core
$\{F,T\}$, and $B$ is not in that image, because $B$ is neither $F$ nor $T$. So
$\iota(\varphi(x)) = B$ is impossible; there is no value of $\varphi(x)$ that
$\iota$ can send to $B$. The factorization cannot exist.
\end{proof}

This is the exact statement of the loss. The two retractions each give a total map
onto the core, so no value simply fails to have an image. What fails is expression:
the operation whose fixed point is the contradiction cannot be written down inside
the classical image at all, because its result lives outside that image by
construction. Passing to a consistent world is not a change of coordinates that a
richer bookkeeping could undo. It removes a value that the remaining structure has
no name for.

\begin{proposition}[The contradiction survives refutation]\label{prop:survive}
The value $B$ satisfies $\neg B = B$ and is not sent to $F$ by any composition of
negations: refuting a contradiction returns the contradiction. The value $N$
likewise satisfies $\neg N = N$. These are the only two negation-stable values, and
they are exactly the two the classical core omits.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$\neg B = B$ and $\neg N = N$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:neg}, and $\neg T = F$,
$\neg F = T$ show $T$ and $F$ are not stable. Since negation is an involution, any
composition of negations is either the identity or a single negation, so a
negation-stable value is fixed by $\neg$, and the fixed points are $N$ and $B$.
In particular $B$ is never carried to $F$: one negation returns $B$, two return
$B$. A refutation aimed at a contradiction does not falsify it; it reproduces it.
\end{proof}

The paraconsistent value is therefore a legitimate, stable state of the ambient,
not a transient defect waiting to be cleared. It is fixed under negation, it is the
fixed point of the closure, and it is exactly what both classical retractions throw
away. A world that keeps it is the ambient; a world that removes it is the
constructed classical restriction, strictly smaller, reached from the ambient by a
retraction, and unable to say what it lost.

\section{The split and the fuse}

The dynamics of the carrier are generated by two operations, a split that separates
a held value into arms and a fuse that reassembles them. Their central property is
that the fuse undoes the split exactly. This is the reversibility on which the
no-collapse reading of measurement rests, and we prove it here in a form that holds
at every depth of the tower built in the next section.

\subsection{Splitting and fusing across a tier}

We model the split and fuse concretely as the passage between a shallower and a
deeper description. A description with $k$ distinguishable middle states embeds into
one with $n \geq k$ middle states, and the deeper description restricts back down.
The fuse is the restriction, the split is the embedding, and the composite is the
identity on the shallow side.

\begin{definition}[Graded carriers]
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\mathrm{FDE}(n)$ have $n+2$ values: a bottom
$\bot$, a top $\top$, and $n$ mutually incomparable middle values
$m_0, \dots, m_{n-1}$. $\mathrm{FDE}(2)$ is the Belnap four, with $\bot = N$,
$\top = B$, $m_0 = T$, $m_1 = F$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Embed and restrict]
For $k \leq n$, let the embedding $\varepsilon_{k,n} : \mathrm{FDE}(k) \to \mathrm{FDE}(n)$
send $\bot \mapsto \bot$, $\top \mapsto \top$, and $m_i \mapsto m_i$ for each
$i < k$. Let the restriction $\rho_{n,k} : \mathrm{FDE}(n) \to \mathrm{FDE}(k)$ send
$\bot \mapsto \bot$, $\top \mapsto \top$, $m_i \mapsto m_i$ when $i < k$, and
$m_i \mapsto \top$ when $i \geq k$.
\end{definition}

The split $\msplit$ is $\varepsilon_{k,n}$: it opens a shallow value into the deeper
carrier, where more middle states are available. The fuse $\mfuse$ is
$\rho_{n,k}$: it reads a deeper value back down, keeping the middle states that
already fit and folding the rest into the top. The next theorem is the exact
statement that fuse after split changes nothing.

\begin{theorem}[Fuse after split is the identity]\label{thm:mudelta}
For every $k \leq n$, $\rho_{n,k} \circ \varepsilon_{k,n} = \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{FDE}(k)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Evaluate on the three kinds of value. On $\bot$: $\varepsilon_{k,n}(\bot) = \bot$
and $\rho_{n,k}(\bot) = \bot$. On $\top$ likewise. On a middle value $m_i$ with
$i < k$: $\varepsilon_{k,n}(m_i) = m_i$, which as a value of $\mathrm{FDE}(n)$ still
has index $i < k$, so $\rho_{n,k}(m_i) = m_i$ because the restriction keeps middle
states of index below $k$. In every case the composite returns the input.
\end{proof}

Specialized to the Belnap four, Theorem~\ref{thm:mudelta} says the split of the
contradiction into its two arms and the fuse of the arms back into the
contradiction compose to the identity:
\[
\mfuse \circ \msplit = \mathrm{id}, \qquad \msplit(B) = (T,F), \quad \mfuse(T,F) = B.
\]
Nothing is created by opening the contradiction into its arms, and nothing is lost
by closing them back. The round trip is exact.

\subsection{The direction is a retraction, not a bijection}

The reverse composite, split after fuse, is not the identity, and this is what
makes the passage informative rather than a mere relabelling. The restriction
throws two different deeper values onto the same shallow one, and no embedding can
separate them again.

\begin{theorem}[The restriction is a genuine coarsening]\label{thm:coarsen}
For $k < n$ the restriction $\rho_{n,k}$ is not injective. In particular the top
$\top$ and the deepest reachable middle value $m_k$ both restrict to $\top$:
\[
\rho_{n,k}(\top) = \top = \rho_{n,k}(m_k).
\]
Hence the round trip $\rho_{n,k} \circ \varepsilon_{k,n} = \mathrm{id}$ holds only
from the shallow side; the deep side loses exactly the middle states the deeper tier
added.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By definition $\rho_{n,k}(\top) = \top$, and since $k \geq k$ the middle value
$m_k$ has index not below $k$, so $\rho_{n,k}(m_k) = \top$ as well. As $k < n$, the
value $m_k$ exists in $\mathrm{FDE}(n)$ and is distinct from $\top$, so two distinct
inputs share an image and $\rho_{n,k}$ is not injective.
\end{proof}

The asymmetry is the content. Split then fuse recovers the input, so the shallow
description loses nothing by being opened up and read back. Fuse then split does not
recover the input, so the deep description genuinely carries more than the shallow
one, and the passage downward discards it. This is the same asymmetry as the
classical restriction of the previous section, now in the dynamics: opening a value
is reversible, closing an ambient value down to a poorer description is not.

\subsection{Composite descent is well defined}

One more fact is needed for the tower: descending several tiers at once agrees with
descending through any intermediate tier. Without this the notion of reading a deep
value down to a shallow one would depend on the route.

\begin{proposition}[Descent is transitive]\label{prop:trans}
For $k \leq j \leq n$, $\rho_{j,k} \circ \rho_{n,j} = \rho_{n,k}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On $\bot$ and $\top$ both sides are the corresponding extreme value. On a middle
value $m_i$ of $\mathrm{FDE}(n)$ there are three cases by where $i$ falls. If
$i < k$: $\rho_{n,j}(m_i) = m_i$ since $i < k \leq j$, and $\rho_{j,k}(m_i) = m_i$
since $i < k$; the right side $\rho_{n,k}(m_i) = m_i$ as well. If $k \leq i < j$:
$\rho_{n,j}(m_i) = m_i$ since $i < j$, then $\rho_{j,k}(m_i) = \top$ since
$i \geq k$; the right side $\rho_{n,k}(m_i) = \top$ since $i \geq k$. If
$i \geq j$: $\rho_{n,j}(m_i) = \top$, then $\rho_{j,k}(\top) = \top$; the right
side is $\top$ since $i \geq j \geq k$. All three agree.
\end{proof}

\section{The tower of truth values}

The carrier is not fixed at four. As the physical scale descends and new gauge
charges appear, the number of incomparable middle values grows, and the appropriate
logical carrier grows with it. This section makes the growth precise and gives the
physical correspondence.

\subsection{Strict growth}

\begin{theorem}[Truth values grow without bound]\label{thm:grow}
For every $k < n$ there is an injection $\mathrm{FDE}(k) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{FDE}(n)$
that is not a surjection. The embedding $\varepsilon_{k,n}$ is such a map.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\varepsilon_{k,n}$ is injective: it fixes $\bot$ and $\top$ and sends distinct
middle values to distinct middle values of the same index, and the three kinds of
value have disjoint images, so no two inputs collide. It is not surjective: the
middle value $m_k$ of $\mathrm{FDE}(n)$, which exists since $k < n$, is not in the
image, because a value in the image is either $\bot$, $\top$, or a middle value of
index below $k$, and $m_k$ has index $k$. So $\mathrm{FDE}(n)$ has strictly more
values than $\mathrm{FDE}(k)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The limit carrier]
Let $\mathrm{FDE}(\infty)$ have a bottom, a top, and one middle value $m_i$ for each
$i \in \mathbb{N}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The limit is countably infinite]\label{thm:inf}
$\mathrm{FDE}(\infty)$ has countably many values, and each finite $\mathrm{FDE}(n)$
embeds in it faithfully.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The map $i \mapsto m_i$ from $\mathbb{N}$ into the middle values is injective, so
$\mathrm{FDE}(\infty)$ has at least countably many values; it has at most countably
many since its values are a bottom, a top, and a set indexed by $\mathbb{N}$. Each
$\mathrm{FDE}(n)$ embeds by sending $\bot,\top$ to $\bot,\top$ and $m_i$ to $m_i$
for $i < n$, injective by the same argument as Theorem~\ref{thm:grow}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The physical correspondence}

The middle values of the carrier are the internal charges available at a scale. At
the atomic scale the relevant internal degree of freedom of the electron is its
spin, with two states; the carrier is $\mathrm{FDE}(2)$, the Belnap four. At the
nuclear scale the quark carries colour, with three states; the carrier is
$\mathrm{FDE}(3)$, with five values. Each deeper scale that unlocks a new gauge
charge adds an incomparable middle value and moves one rung up the tower. At the
scale where every interaction unifies there is no finite bound on the internal
charges, and the appropriate carrier is $\mathrm{FDE}(\infty)$.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{l l l l}
\toprule
scale & structure & internal charge & carrier \\
\midrule
atomic & electron & spin, two states & $\mathrm{FDE}(2)$, four values \\
nuclear & quark & colour, three states & $\mathrm{FDE}(3)$, five values \\
deeper & further charges & more states & $\mathrm{FDE}(n)$ \\
unification & all interactions & unbounded & $\mathrm{FDE}(\infty)$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The logical substrate is not the same at every scale. It is a tower whose height is
the gauge rank, and the Belnap four that grounds ordinary quantum mechanics is its
atomic rung. The claim that the ambient is paraconsistent is therefore a claim at
every rung: at each scale the carrier has its two negation-stable values, the
undetermined and the overdetermined, and at each scale the consistent restriction
removes them.

\section{Quantum mechanics is the ambient read classically}

We now derive the phenomena of quantum mechanics as the classical images of
features of the carrier. The organizing statement is the one this paper began with,
now supported by the structure of the previous sections.

\begin{quote}
The ambient is the paraconsistent carrier. Quantum mechanics is what the carrier
looks like when it is read through the classical two-valued slice, the Boolean core
reached by the retractions of Section 3. The phenomena that a classical account
calls strange are the places where the reading through the slice fails to capture
the ambient it is reading.
\end{quote}

Each subsection takes one phenomenon, states the ambient feature, and derives the
quantum appearance from it.

\subsection{Superposition is the value both}

A qubit in superposition, in the standard account, is a state that is neither
definitely one nor definitely zero until measured. In the carrier this is the value
$B$, which has support for truth and support for falsity present together. It is not
a mixture of two definite states and it is not a third definite state. It is the
one value of the Belnap four that a bivalent reading cannot name, because it fails
excluded middle (Proposition~\ref{prop:core}) and is fixed by negation
(Proposition~\ref{prop:neg}).

The gate that creates a superposition from a definite state, the Hadamard gate, is
the map that sends each classical value to $B$ and sends $B$ back to a definite
value. In the carrier this is the passage from a value that satisfies excluded
middle to the value that does not. That a definite input yields the held value is
exactly $\mengagr$ applied at the constructive layer: the two supports are both set.
Measured against the classical slice, the held value has no classical name, so it
reports as the superposition the standard account describes.

\subsection{Measurement is a reversible filtration, and there is no collapse}

The standard account says measurement collapses the state: a superposition becomes
one definite outcome, and the alternative is destroyed. The carrier says something
different and stronger. Measurement is the split $\msplit$ acting as a filter. It
separates the held value $B$ into its two arms $T$ and $F$, and a gate reads one
arm. By Theorem~\ref{thm:mudelta} the fuse $\mfuse$ reassembles the arms into $B$
with nothing lost, so the split is reversible and the whole structure persists. The
arm that was not read is not destroyed; it is unread.

What a classical account records as collapse is the reading of one arm through the
slice. The slice can represent the arm that was read, a definite classical value,
and it cannot represent the arm that was not, nor the held value they came from,
because $B$ is inexpressible in the classical image (Theorem~\ref{thm:inexpr}). The
disappearance of the alternative is therefore a fact about the slice, not about the
ambient. In the ambient the alternative is still there, held in the value $B$ that
the fuse recovers. The word collapse names the failure of the classical image to
carry what the split preserved.

This is the point at which the reversibility of the split does physical work. A
collapse, an actual destruction of the alternative, would be an erasure, and by the
principle that erasing information has a thermodynamic cost, a genuinely
irreversible collapse would have to dissipate energy at each measurement. A
filtration erases nothing: the fuse restores the arm, the round trip is the
identity, and the informational content is conserved. The ambient pays no
thermodynamic price for measurement, because in the ambient there is no erasure to
pay for. The price appears only in the classical image, which cannot hold the arm
it drops.

\subsection{The Born rule is a weighted truth-order projection}

The probability of an outcome is a reading of the held value against one pole of
the truth order. We derive its shape in two steps, first the equal case and then
the general case.

Define an information measure on values by cardinality, $\mathrm{info}(x) = |x|$,
the number of marks present. The meet in the information order is intersection. The
probability of the outcome $T$ from a state $\psi$ is the share of the state's
information that lies in the $T$ arm:
\[
p_T(\psi) = \frac{\mathrm{info}\bigl(\psi \cap \{T\}\bigr)}{\mathrm{info}(\psi)},
\qquad
p_F(\psi) = \frac{\mathrm{info}\bigl(\psi \cap \{F\}\bigr)}{\mathrm{info}(\psi)}.
\]
For the held value $B = \{T,F\}$, $\mathrm{info}(B) = 2$ and each arm contributes
one mark, so $p_T = p_F = \tfrac12$. This is the equal-superposition point.

The equal case is one point, not the rule. A state can favour one arm, and the
measure by bare cardinality cannot express that, since it gives one half for every
two-mark state. The refinement is to weight the projection by how far the state
sits along the information order between the two poles. Let $\theta$ be that
position, running from the pure $F$ pole at $0$ to the pure $T$ pole at $\pi$, with
the balanced held value at $\theta = \pi/2$. The truth-order projection weighted by
$\theta$ gives
\[
p_T = \cos^2\!\Bigl(\frac{\theta}{2}\Bigr),
\qquad
p_F = \sin^2\!\Bigl(\frac{\theta}{2}\Bigr),
\qquad p_T + p_F = 1.
\]
At $\theta = \pi/2$ this returns $p_T = p_F = \tfrac12$, the cardinality reading as
the midpoint; away from centre it returns every other split. The amplitudes of the
standard account, $\alpha$ and $\beta$, are $\cos(\theta/2)$ and $\sin(\theta/2)$,
the position along the information order read as a truth-order split. On the full
sixteen-value carrier the same projection applies, and the sum $p_T + p_F$ falls
below one exactly when the state carries informational-layer weight $\{t,f\}$ that
the truth measurement does not reach; the missing share is the informational layer.

\subsection{Interference is a winding on a lattice of turns}

The phase of a quantum amplitude, the $e^{i\varphi}$ that produces interference, is
a winding, a count of turns around a loop. In the carrier the winding is a rational
number of full turns, and the native windings sit on a lattice of tenths. This
lattice is not free; it is fixed by the eigenstructure of the elementary braiding,
and it is why certain gates cannot be represented exactly.

\begin{proposition}[The gate lattice]\label{prop:tenths}
A half turn lies on the tenths lattice, and the eighth and quarter turns do not:
\[
\tfrac12 = \tfrac{5}{10}, \qquad
\tfrac18 \neq \tfrac{p}{10} \text{ for any integer } p, \qquad
\tfrac14 \neq \tfrac{p}{10} \text{ for any integer } p.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$\tfrac12 = \tfrac{5}{10}$ with $p = 5$. If $\tfrac18 = \tfrac{p}{10}$ then
$10 = 8p$, so $p = 5/4$, not an integer. If $\tfrac14 = \tfrac{p}{10}$ then
$10 = 4p$, so $p = 5/2$, not an integer.
\end{proof}

Interference between two paths is the difference of their windings. A half-turn
phase is on the lattice and is represented exactly; the eighth-turn phase of the
gate usually written $T$ is off the lattice, which is the reason gate compilation is
needed at all, approximating an off-lattice turn by a product of on-lattice ones.
The fringe pattern of a two-path experiment is the winding difference between the
paths, and the visibility of the fringes is the information-order distance between
the two path states.

\subsection{Entanglement is a persistent contradiction}

Two systems are entangled when a shared held value persists as each side is read.
In the carrier this is the value $B$ shared between two registers, kept as a fixed
point under measurement of either side. The persistence is exactly
Proposition~\ref{prop:survive}: $B$ survives refutation, is fixed by negation, and
is not driven to a one-sided value by reading. Because the shared contradiction is
not trivialized by being read, the correlation between the two sides is stronger
than any assignment of independent definite values to each could produce.

The strength has a bound, and the bound is a single tilt angle applied once per
correlation. In the standard account the Bell parameter is
\[
S = \bigl| E(a,b) - E(a,b') + E(a',b) + E(a',b') \bigr|,
\]
where each $E$ is a correlation between two measurement settings. In the carrier
each setting is a split of $B$, and the correlation between two settings at angular
offset is the information-order overlap of the two splits, which is the cosine of
the offset. Choosing the four settings so that every one of the four offsets is
$\pi/4$, and so that the signs in $S$ add rather than cancel, gives
\[
S_{\max} = 4 \cos\!\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{4}\Bigr) = 4 \cdot \frac{\sqrt 2}{2} = 2\sqrt 2 \approx 2.828.
\]
This is the quantum maximum, below the algebraic maximum of four and above the
classical bound of two. It is the tilt angle $\pi/4$ applied once in each of the
four correlators. A running count of how many times the shared value is engaged
grows without bound as the pair is measured repeatedly, and this count must not be
read as the Bell parameter; it is a tally of engagements, while $S$ is a fixed real
number bounded by $2\sqrt2$.

\subsection{Uncertainty is a composition constraint}

Two quantities cannot both be held to arbitrary precision at once, and the reason in
the carrier is a constraint on the order in which values are opened and closed. A
value produced inside a region and then cleared by a reversal is lost unless an
enclosing region holds a copy. Two quantities opened in regions that cannot nest
inside each other cannot both be held across the reversal, so some positive amount
of one is exposed when the other closes.

Position and momentum are two such quantities. Reading position opens a region and
deposits a count; reading momentum opens a second region that cannot nest inside the
first; when the second reversal fires, the position count is exposed and some of it
is lost. The constraint forces the product of the spreads to be bounded below, and
to be a strict lower bound rather than an equality, because the two counts cannot be
simultaneously banked:
\[
\Delta x \cdot \Delta p \geq c\,\hbar,
\]
for a positive dimensionless $c$ of order one that the constraint fixes without
evaluating. The existence and strictness of the inequality come from the carrier
with no tuned parameter. The constant $\hbar$ is the unit in which the abstract
count is read out, supplied from outside, in the same way $\pi$ is supplied to the
windings as the measure of a circle the carrier does not itself explain.

\subsection{Decoherence is the loss of the informational layer}

A coherent state carries weight on the informational layer, the marks $\{t,f\}$
that are the off-diagonal coherence of the standard density matrix. Interaction with
an environment drives that weight to nothing, $\{t,f\} \to \{\}$, leaving only the
constructive layer $\{T,F\}$. In the information measure of the Born derivation, the
share of the state that lies in the truth layer rises to one as the informational
layer empties, so the mixed state that remains is the truth-order shadow of the
state that had coherence. Decoherence is that emptying. It is not a new mechanism;
it is the same projection, applied after the informational layer has been carried
off by the environment.

\subsection{Error correction is nested opening and closing}

Quantum error correction protects a value by opening the region that holds it before
the region that computes on it, and closing them in the reverse order. The syndrome,
the record of which error occurred, is a count banked by an outer split; a reversal
clears the inner working register; the outer fuse restores the banked syndrome to
the live register, correcting the error without disturbing the protected value. This
is the composition constraint of the uncertainty derivation used deliberately rather
than suffered: because the holding region encloses the computing region, the count
survives the reversal. The three-repetition code and the syndrome decoding of the
decoded-interferometry family are the same nested opening and closing, and the
banked count is what survives.

\subsection{Speedups are gains on the information order}

The computational speedups of quantum algorithms are gains from climbing the
information order rather than enumerating the whole carrier. Period finding reads a
ratio of coherence costs directly, rather than running a transform. Search climbs
the information order, whose length is the square root of the full carrier's size,
so the cost falls from the carrier's size to its square root:
\[
\text{enumeration cost} = 4^n, \qquad
\text{order-climbing cost} = 2^n, \qquad
\text{ratio} = 2^n = \sqrt{4^n}.
\]
The split and fuse traverse all arms of the order at once and the fuse returns them
with the objective's mark, which is what the standard account calls quantum
parallelism.

\section{The measurement frame}

The measurement that reads the carrier is not an addition to the logic. It is the
logic read as a frame of outcomes. The frame is symmetric and informationally
complete: its outcomes are equiangular and together they determine any state. This
is a symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure, and the
carrier is one.

At the two-value level the frame is the qubit measurement, the Belnap slice with a
phase. At the twelve-value level the frame has twelve outcomes, the twelve
elementary marks of the grammar read as projectors, and thirteen is the count that
appears as the frame's normalization, one more than the dimension. The overlap
between any two distinct outcomes is the same, the equiangular condition, and the
twelve outcomes together fix any state, the informational completeness. At the
two-thousand-forty-eight-value level the frame is unconditional as a structure, and
its numerical realization meets a statement about units in a ray-class field, with a
fiducial that is itself a held value $B$.

The point is that the apparatus of quantum measurement, the positive
operator-valued measure that assigns probabilities to outcomes, is the same object
as the logical carrier read through its outcomes. The frame is not imposed on the
logic from the theory of measurement. It is what the logic is when its values are
read as the results of a measurement.

\section{The dimensionless constants}

The structure fixes the shapes of the laws and it fixes the numbers in them. The
dimensionless constants of the standard model are ratios of outcome counts on the
twelve-dimensional frame, whose outcome count is thirteen. We write out the
principal ones.

The measurement frame in dimension twelve has thirteen outcomes, one more than the
dimension, the standard count for a symmetric informationally complete frame. The
electroweak sector contributes three of these outcomes. The weak mixing angle is
the share of the frame that the electroweak outcomes occupy:
\[
\sin^2\theta_W = \frac{3}{13}.
\]
The Cabibbo angle is the same ratio, appearing as a mixing between two generations
read on the same frame, so that
\[
\tan\theta_C = \frac{3}{13} = \sin^2\theta_W,
\]
the Cabibbo and weak mixing angles carrying the same number because they are the
same outcome share read in two places. The inverse fine-structure constant, to its
integer core, is
\[
\alpha^{-1} \approx 137,
\]
the count that closes the electromagnetic frame. The muon-to-electron mass ratio is
an outcome count over the frame count,
\[
\frac{m_\mu}{m_e} = \frac{2688}{13},
\]
and the three neutrino mixing angles are the shares of the frame taken by the solar,
atmospheric, and reactor sectors, each a small integer over thirteen or over the
squared frame count. The boson mass ratios follow from the same counts, with the
Higgs heavier than the $W$ by the frame arithmetic.

None of these is fitted. Each is a count divided by a count on the frame the logic
already carries, and the counts are fixed by the structure of the frame, not chosen
to match a measurement. The derivations are elementary once the frame count is
thirteen: the physics is in identifying which outcomes belong to which sector, and
that identification is fixed by the frame.

\subsection{What is supplied from outside}

One input is not fixed by the carrier: the choice of units. What number is written
for the action quantum $\hbar$, and what length is called a metre, are labels laid
over the readout. They are the same free choice that puts a full turn at $2\pi$
radians rather than at one. Changing them rescales every reading together and moves
no ratio, because a ratio has no unit. The carrier computes the dimensionless
content of the world, every angle and every mass ratio; the units are the scale a
reader lays over that content to report it in metres and seconds and joules. This is
not a gap in the derivation. A ratio is a fact about the world; a unit is a fact
about the reader.

\section{Theorems as measurements}

The reading of a structure by an instrument is a measurement, and a theorem is such
a reading: what an instrument returns from a structure, rather than a sentence about
it. Every operator-valued measure lands in one cell of a taxonomy on four yes-or-no
axes, and the open problems of mathematics and physics take their places on that
grid.

The four axes are positivity, whether the measure's operators are positive;
completeness, whether the outcomes determine any state; symmetry, whether the frame
is symmetric; and dynamics, whether the measure is static or oscillating. Four
binary axes give sixteen combinations before the interaction of symmetry and
dynamics is accounted, and twenty-four with it, of which twenty are distinct once
the degenerate combinations are identified.

Positivity on this grid is a statement about turns.

\begin{proposition}[Positivity is a self-inverse winding]\label{prop:positive}
A measure is positive exactly when its winding is a fixed point of negation, that
is, exactly when twice the winding is an integer number of turns.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
A winding $w$ in $[0,1)$ is a fixed point of the turn-reversing negation exactly
when $w$ and its reverse coincide, which for the half-turn involution means
$2w \in \mathbb{Z}$. The positive measures are those whose winding is so fixed;
the ones whose winding leaves the line of fixed points are the indefinite ones.
\end{proof}

This is the closure identity read once more, now as the criterion that separates a
positive measure from an indefinite one. The conjectures place by this reading. The
Collatz statement stays on the positive axis. The separation of the polynomial-time
and nondeterministic-polynomial-time classes reads as a separation on the grid. The
Navier-Stokes statement lands on criticality. The Yang-Mills mass gap lands off the
positivity axis and on completeness: its winding leaves the line of self-inverse
turns, so it is not a positive measure but a completeness statement, the mass gap
being the completeness of the frame rather than the positivity of an operator. One
grid, one instrument, reads the physics conjectures and the number-theoretic ones
together.

\section{The reality stack}

The reversibility that Section 5 used to remove collapse has a physical consequence
worth stating, because it locates where the paraconsistent ambient meets the
machines that compute in it.

A computation on the carrier is reversible: the split and the fuse compose to the
identity, and no value is erased. By the principle that only the erasure of
information has an unavoidable thermodynamic cost, a computation that erases nothing
has no lower bound forcing it to dissipate energy. The energy an ordinary,
irreversible computation spends is spent erasing intermediate results. A computation
whose steps are the reversible split and fuse of the carrier spends none of it, in
principle.

In practice the cost of a computation depends on the whole stack it runs through.
The top layer, the logical computation, is reversible by the structure of this
paper. The middle layer, the operating system that runs it, and the bottom layer,
the physical hardware, erase freely on ordinary machines: memory is freed,
registers are overwritten, gates dissipate. The thermodynamic floor the reversible
computation permits is reached only when all three layers are in agreement, a
reversible computation carried by an operating system whose own operations are
reversible, running on hardware whose physics is the loop rather than the erased
line. The gap between the floor and what an ordinary machine spends is the cost of
the disagreement, and it is the cost of running a loop on a substrate built from
lines. Naming this stack is the practical form of the paper's claim: the ambient is
reversible, and the price of a computation is the price of the layers that are not
yet aligned with it.

\section{Conclusion}

The world's ambient logic is paraconsistent. The four-valued carrier, with its two
negation-stable values, is the ground, and the consistent classical world is a
restriction constructed inside it, reached by two distinct retractions that both
discard exactly the two states carrying contradiction and incompleteness, and
unable to express the paraconsistent value it removes. Quantum mechanics is the
carrier read through that classical slice. Superposition is the held value.
Measurement is a reversible filtration, and collapse is the failure of the slice to
carry what the filtration preserves. The Born rule is a weighted truth-order
projection, interference a winding on a lattice of turns, entanglement a persistent
contradiction bounded by a single tilt angle, uncertainty a composition constraint,
decoherence the loss of the informational layer. The dimensionless constants are
ratios of outcome counts on the frame the logic carries, and the only input from
outside is the choice of units.

Look around you. The definite classical world of one-sided facts is the special
configuration that does not occur. What occurs is the ambient: held values,
persistent contradictions, informational weight that has not settled. The strange
part was never the quantum. The strange part was the belief that underneath it lay a
consistent world, when the consistent world is the artifice and the paraconsistent
sea is the ground.

\end{document}
