\title{\bfseries Usurping Quantum Mechanics II\\[0.3em]
\large Tensor Filtration and the Paraconsistent Original}
\author{C. Lando Mills\\ \small Trabuco Canyon, California}
\date{3 September 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\noindent
Quantum mechanics is the classical-logical image of a paraconsistent four-valued
logic. The first part of this program established the direction: the ambient of the
world is the paraconsistent trilattice, and the consistent classical world is a
restriction cut out of it by two retractions that discard the states carrying
contradiction. This second part carries the mechanics. It develops the operation at
the center of the account, tensor filtration, as an explicit ladder of raising,
lowering, and diagonal operators on the weight sectors of an $m$-fold register, and
shows that measurement is filtration through this ladder rather than any collapse.
It then folds in a complete worked instance. The problem of Optimal Polynomial
Intersection has a quantum algorithm, Decoded Quantum Interferometry, whose expected
performance is governed by the largest eigenvalue of a finite tridiagonal matrix. We
show that this matrix is the classical-logical image of a paraconsistent word: the
word's own split, fuse, and evaluate marks, realized on the $m$-fold register, are
exactly the raising operator, its adjoint the lowering operator, and the diagonal
operator whose entries are that matrix, term for term. The algorithm's expectation
value is the paraconsistent object read through the coreflector. We compute both the
finite operator-valued value and its asymptotic scalar limit directly, and measure,
across four scales, the richer finite-size description collapsing monotonically onto
the poorer limit, the same direction the coreflector always moves, measured rather
than assumed. Three descriptions of one object, the paraconsistent, the
classical-logical, and the asymptotic, lock together.
\end{abstract}

\tableofcontents

\section{Introduction}

The claim of this program is that the world's ambient logic is paraconsistent, a
four-valued logic in which a proposition can carry support for its truth and support
for its falsity at once, and that quantum mechanics is what that logic looks like
when it is read through the classical two-valued slice. The consistent classical
world is a restriction constructed inside the paraconsistent ambient, reached by a
retraction that discards the states carrying contradiction, and strictly smaller
than the ambient it is cut from. The world does not appear classical at any scale;
the classical description is a bookkeeping laid over the ambient that declines to
look at the structure constituting it.

The first part of this program set the direction and derived the phenomena of
quantum mechanics as classical images of features of the carrier. This second part
does two things the first did not.

First, it develops the mechanics of the operation at the center of the account.
Measurement in this program is not a collapse; it is a tensor filtration, a
reversible selection of one factor of a tensor while the others remain. This part
makes the filtration concrete as an explicit ladder of operators on the weight
sectors of a many-coordinate register: a raising operator that opens a value into
more support, a lowering operator that is its adjoint, and a diagonal operator that
reads support already present. The three are the split, the fuse, and the evaluate
marks of the grammar, realized as linear operators, and together they are a
tridiagonal matrix whose structure is the whole content of the filtration.

Second, it folds in a complete worked instance in which the classical-logical image
of a paraconsistent object is not only exhibited but computed and measured. The
problem is Optimal Polynomial Intersection, a hard combinatorial optimization over a
finite field. Its state-of-the-art quantum algorithm, Decoded Quantum
Interferometry, has an expected performance governed by the largest eigenvalue of a
finite tridiagonal matrix. We show that this matrix is exactly the ladder of the
previous paragraph, the classical-logical image of a paraconsistent word, and that
the algorithm's expectation value is that word read through the coreflector. We then
compute the finite operator-valued value and its asymptotic scalar limit and measure
the one collapsing onto the other across four scales, the richer description giving
way to the poorer in the exact direction the coreflector moves.

We do not treat the dimensionless constants here; that thread belongs to the first
part. The spine of this part is the filtration mechanics and the worked convergence,
and everything is proved or computed on the page.

\section{The carrier}

We recall the carrier compactly, since the mechanics needs its operations but not a
second full development.

First-Degree Entailment separates the support for a proposition's truth from the
support for its falsity, giving four base answers: true only, false only, both, and
neither, written $T$, $F$, $B$, $N$. The trilattice of Shramko, Dunn and
Takenaka~\cite{sdt} adds an informational layer of an acceptable value $t$ and a
rejectable value $f$, and the carrier is the sixteen subsets of $\{T,F,t,f\}$. Three
orders act on it: the information order $\leqi$, subset inclusion, along which a
value only gains content; the truth order $\leqt$, along which truth support grows
and falsity support shrinks; and the constructivity order $\leqc$, along which the
settled layer grows and the informational layer shrinks. Negation $\neg$ exchanges
$T$ with $F$ and $t$ with $f$; it is an involution whose two fixed points are $N$ and
$B$, the two values that fail the classical law of excluded middle. The Belnap four
$\{N,T,F,B\}$ is the classical slice of the carrier, the part whose informational
layer is empty.

The truth order on the Belnap four is $F \leqt N \leqt T$ and $F \leqt B \leqt T$
with $N$ and $B$ incomparable, so $F$ is the bottom and $T$ the top and the two
nonclassical values sit between them on separate rungs. The value $B$ satisfies
$B \wedge_{\mathrm t} \neg B = B$ and $B \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg B = B$, so a
contradiction met or joined with its own negation is the contradiction and does not
reach falsity or truth. This is the paraconsistency: a contradiction is held as a
value rather than exploding the logic.

\section{The classical restriction}

The passage to a consistent world is a retraction onto the Boolean core, and it is
lossy in a precise sense we prove here, because the worked instance below is a
measurement of exactly this loss.

\begin{definition}[Boolean core]
Let $\mathbf{B} = \{F,T\}$, the two one-sided Belnap values, with the inherited truth
order and negation. It is the two-element Boolean algebra, and it is exactly the set
of Belnap values satisfying $x \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg x = T$.
\end{definition}

The values failing excluded middle are $N$ and $B$, computed from the truth-order
join: $N \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg N = N$ and $B \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg B = B$, neither
equal to $T$, while $T \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg T = T$ and $F \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg F = T$.

\begin{definition}[The two collapses]
Let the ex falso map $c$ and the ex quodlibet map $r$ from the Belnap four to
$\mathbf{B}$ be
\[
c(T)=T,\; c(F)=F,\; c(N)=F,\; c(B)=F, \qquad
r(T)=T,\; r(F)=F,\; r(N)=T,\; r(B)=T,
\]
and let $\iota : \mathbf{B} \hookrightarrow \{N,T,F,B\}$ be the inclusion.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The core is reached by two distinct adjunctions]\label{thm:two}
$c$ is monotone, restricts to the identity on $\mathbf{B}$, and is right adjoint to
the inclusion in the truth order, $\iota(x) \leqt v \iff x \leqt c(v)$. $r$ is
monotone, restricts to the identity on $\mathbf{B}$, and is left adjoint to the
inclusion, $r(v) \leqt x \iff v \leqt \iota(x)$. The two are distinct, differing on
the nonclassical values, $r(N)=r(B)=T \neq F = c(N)=c(B)$, and agreeing on
$\mathbf{B}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Monotonicity of $c$: the truth-order covers $F \leqt N$, $F \leqt B$, $N \leqt T$,
$B \leqt T$ map under $c$ to $F \leqt F$, $F \leqt F$, $F \leqt T$, $F \leqt T$, all
true. The adjunction has two cases. For $x=F$, both $x \leqt c(v)$ and
$\iota(x) \leqt v$ hold for every $v$, since $F$ is the truth-order bottom. For
$x=T$, $x \leqt c(v)$ forces $c(v)=T$, which holds exactly when $v=T$, and
$\iota(T) \leqt v$ forces $v=T$; equivalent. For $r$: the covers map under $r$ to
$F \leqt T$, $F \leqt T$, $T \leqt T$, $T \leqt T$, all true. For $x=T$ both sides
hold for every $v$; for $x=F$, $r(v) \leqt F$ forces $r(v)=F$, holding exactly when
$v=F$, and $v \leqt \iota(F)=F$ forces $v=F$; equivalent. Distinctness is direct from
the definitions.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Neither is an information-order adjunction]\label{thm:noinfo}
In the information order, where $N$ is the bottom and $B$ the top with $T$ and $F$
between, neither $c$ nor $r$ is adjoint to $\iota$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Were $r$ left adjoint in $\leqi$, then with $v=B$, $x=T$ we would need
$r(B) \leqi T \iff B \leqi \iota(T)=T$; the right side is false ($B$ is the top),
the left side $T \leqi T$ true. Were $c$ right adjoint, with $v=N$, $x=F$ we would
need $F \leqi N \iff \iota(F) \leqi c(N)$; the left side is false ($N$ the bottom),
issues split, so no adjunction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The collapse is exactly lossy]\label{thm:lossy}
Let $\mathrm{inc}$ be the closure operator on the Belnap four that sends every value
to $B$. It is idempotent with unique fixed point $B$, and it cannot be factored
through the classical inclusion: there is no map $\varphi : \mathbf{B} \to \mathbf{B}$
with $\iota \circ \varphi = \mathrm{inc} \circ \iota$. The paraconsistent value $B$
is inexpressible inside either classical image.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\mathrm{inc}(\mathrm{inc}(x)) = \mathrm{inc}(B) = B = \mathrm{inc}(x)$, and a fixed
point solves $x=B$, so $B$ is unique. If $\varphi$ existed, then for classical $x$,
$\iota(\varphi(x)) = \mathrm{inc}(\iota(x)) = B$; but $\iota$ has image
$\{F,T\}$, which does not contain $B$, so $\iota(\varphi(x))=B$ is impossible. No
such $\varphi$ exists.
\end{proof}

The two retractions each give a total map onto the core, so no value is left without
an image, and yet the operation whose fixed point is the contradiction cannot be
written inside the image. The passage to a consistent world does not lose a value by
sending it nowhere; it loses the ability to name the state that carries
contradiction. The worked instance below measures exactly how much a specific
paraconsistent object exceeds its two classical retractions, and finds the excess
positive at every finite size and shrinking toward the retraction as the size grows.

\section{Tensor filtration}

The operation at the center of the account is the split and its adjoint fuse, and
their action on a many-coordinate register is a ladder of operators that we now
build explicitly. This is the mechanics that measurement, and the worked instance,
run on.

\subsection{The register and its weight sectors}

Take $m$ copies of the constructive layer, an $m$-coordinate register in which each
coordinate carries a one-sided value, $T$ or $F$. A basis state is a string
$x \in \{T,F\}^m$. The \emph{weight} of a string is the number of coordinates at
$T$, and the \emph{weight-$k$ sector} is the set of strings of weight $k$, of which
there are $\binom{m}{k}$.

\begin{definition}[Uniform sector states]
For $0 \leq k \leq m$ let
\[
\ket{k} = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2} \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k} \ket{x}
\]
be the uniform normalized superposition of the weight-$k$ strings. The
$\ket{k}$ for $k=0,\dots,m$ are orthonormal, and they span the symmetric subspace of
the register, the part invariant under permuting the coordinates.
\end{definition}

The uniform sector states are the natural coordinates for a filtration that does not
distinguish the coordinates from one another, which is the symmetric case the worked
instance needs.

\subsection{Split as raising, fuse as lowering}

The split $\msplit$ opens a value into more support: on the register it takes a
coordinate that is at $F$ and sets it to $T$, adding one to the weight. Applied
symmetrically, summed over the coordinates that can be raised, it is the raising
operator.

\begin{theorem}[The ladder operators]\label{thm:ladder}
Let $S_{+}$ be the operator that sends a string of weight $k$ to the sum of its
weight-$(k+1)$ extensions, each obtained by raising one coordinate from $F$ to $T$,
and let $S_{-}$ be its adjoint. On the uniform sector states,
\[
S_{+}\ket{k} = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}\,\ket{k+1},
\qquad
S_{-}\ket{k} = \sqrt{k(m-k+1)}\,\ket{k-1}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $\ket{k} = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}\sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k}\ket{x}$. Acting with
$S_{+}$, each weight-$k$ string $x$ maps to the sum of the $m-k$ strings obtained by
raising one of its $F$ coordinates, so
\[
S_{+}\ket{k} = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2} \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k}\ \sum_{i:\,x_i=F} \ket{x^{(i)}},
\]
where $x^{(i)}$ raises coordinate $i$. Each weight-$(k+1)$ string $y$ arises in this
double sum once for each of its $k+1$ coordinates at $T$, since lowering any one of
them gives a weight-$k$ string $x$ that raises back to $y$. So the coefficient of
$\ket{y}$ is $(k+1)\binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}$, and
\[
S_{+}\ket{k} = (k+1)\binom{m}{k}^{-1/2} \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(y)=k+1}\ket{y}
= (k+1)\binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}\binom{m}{k+1}^{1/2}\ket{k+1}.
\]
Using $\binom{m}{k+1}/\binom{m}{k} = (m-k)/(k+1)$, the coefficient is
$(k+1)\sqrt{(m-k)/(k+1)} = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$, giving the first identity. The second
is the adjoint: $S_{-}$ is defined by
$\langle k-1 \mid S_{-} \mid k\rangle = \langle k \mid S_{+} \mid k-1\rangle^{*}
= \sqrt{k(m-k+1)}$, using the first identity with $k$ replaced by $k-1$, so
$S_{-}\ket{k} = \sqrt{k(m-k+1)}\,\ket{k-1}$.
\end{proof}

The split $\msplit$ is $S_{+}$, opening one coordinate into truth support; the fuse
$\mfuse$ is $S_{-}$, its adjoint, closing one coordinate back. The two are a raising
and lowering pair on the ladder of weight sectors, and their composition returns the
sector it started from up to the ladder coefficients, the operator form of the
counit-unit law that opening and closing lose nothing.

\subsection{Evaluate as the diagonal}

The evaluate mark $\mevalt$ reads truth support already present, depositing a fixed
amount once for each coordinate at $T$.

\begin{proposition}[The diagonal operator]\label{prop:diag}
Let $D$ be the operator that, for a fixed real $d$, reads $d$ once for each
coordinate at $T$. On the uniform sector states $D\ket{k} = kd\,\ket{k}$, diagonal
in the sector basis.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On a string $x$ of weight $k$, $D$ reads $d$ once per $T$ coordinate, so
$D\ket{x} = kd\ket{x}$. Since every string in $\ket{k}$ has weight $k$, $D$ acts as
the scalar $kd$ on the whole uniform superposition, $D\ket{k}=kd\ket{k}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The ladder is a tridiagonal matrix}

The three operators together, the split-raising, the fuse-lowering, and the
evaluate-diagonal, form one operator on the ladder of $\ell+1$ lowest sectors.

\begin{theorem}[The filtration matrix]\label{thm:matrix}
On the span of $\ket{0},\dots,\ket{\ell}$, the operator $A = D + S_{+} + S_{-}$ is the
$(\ell+1)\times(\ell+1)$ real symmetric tridiagonal matrix with diagonal entries
$A_{kk} = kd$ for $k=0,\dots,\ell$ and off-diagonal entries
$A_{k,k+1} = A_{k+1,k} = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Proposition~\ref{prop:diag} the diagonal is $D\ket{k}=kd\ket{k}$, giving
$A_{kk}=kd$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:ladder} the raising and lowering give
$A_{k+1,k} = \langle k+1\mid S_{+}\mid k\rangle = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$ and
$A_{k,k+1} = \langle k\mid S_{-}\mid k+1\rangle = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$, equal, so the
matrix is symmetric. All other entries vanish because $S_{\pm}$ change the weight by
one and $D$ preserves it, so only the diagonal and the first off-diagonals are
nonzero.
\end{proof}

This tridiagonal matrix is the whole content of the filtration. It is built from the
three marks alone, the split and its adjoint on the off-diagonal and the evaluate on
the diagonal, and it is the object whose spectrum the worked instance reads. The
filtration is reversible in the sense already fixed: the off-diagonal part is a
raising and lowering pair, adjoint to each other, and the diagonal part is
self-adjoint, so $A$ is self-adjoint and generates a reversible motion on the ladder.

\subsection{Measurement is filtration through the ladder}

Measurement selects a sector. The split opens the register up the ladder, a chosen
sector is read, and the fuse closes it back, and because the fuse is the adjoint of
the split the whole ladder persists through the reading. What a classical account
records as a collapse to a definite weight is the reading of one rung of the ladder
while the ladder remains, and the rungs not read are the tensor factors the split
opened and the fuse can restore. There is no collapse in the ladder; there is a
filtration that selects a rung and a fuse that recovers the whole. The apparent
destruction of the other rungs is the classical slice's inability to carry more than
the one it read, the same inexpressibility as Theorem~\ref{thm:lossy}, now at the
level of the register rather than the single value.

\section{Measurement, superposition, and the phenomena}

Before the worked instance, we place the phenomena on the ladder, briefly, since the
mechanics above is what they run on.

Superposition is the held value $B$, true and false together, its own negation, the
one Belnap value the classical slice cannot name. On the register it is a state
spread across weight sectors rather than sitting in one, the uniform sector states
being its symmetric instances.

Measurement is filtration through the ladder, as above, with no collapse. The word
tensor is exact: the split opens a value into a pair of tensor factors, a reading
selects one factor while the other remains a factor of the whole, and the fuse
recombines them. Reading $x \otimes y$ reads $x$ without deleting $y$; the classical
account writes only the read factor and calls the loss of the other collapse. Because
the fuse is the adjoint of the split and the round trip is the identity, the ambient
pays no thermodynamic price for measurement; a genuine collapse would be an erasure
with a Landauer cost~\cite{landauer}, and the filtration erases nothing, in the sense
made concrete by reversible computing~\cite{bennett,fredkin}.

The Born rule is the overlap of a state with a rung. For the two-outcome case, a
pure state at polar angle $\theta$ from the true pole is
$\cos(\theta/2)\ket{T} + e^{i\varphi}\sin(\theta/2)\ket{F}$, the half-angle from the
ray double cover, and the probability of the true outcome is
$|\langle T \mid \psi\rangle|^2 = \cos^2(\theta/2)$. The quadratic form is forced,
not chosen: a probability assignment on a positive-operator frame that is additive
and non-contextual has the form $\mathrm{tr}(\rho E)$ by Busch's
theorem~\cite{busch}, extending Gleason's~\cite{gleason} to every dimension including
two, and on the truth projector this is $\cos^2(\theta/2)$.

Entanglement is a shared held value that persists as each part is read, and the
strength of the correlation it produces is bounded by a single tilt angle: choosing
the four Bell settings~\cite{bell,chsh} at offsets of $\pi/4$ gives
$S = 4\cos(\pi/4) = 2\sqrt2$, the Tsirelson bound~\cite{tsirelson}, the shared value
supplying exactly $\cos(\pi/4)$ per setting. Decoherence is the emptying of the
informational layer $\{t,f\}$ to the environment, the coherences of the density
matrix carried off while the populations, the diagonal read by the sector projection,
remain.

\section{A worked realization: Optimal Polynomial Intersection}

We now carry a complete instance in which the classical-logical image of a
paraconsistent object is computed and its convergence to the paraconsistent original
measured. The object is the tridiagonal filtration matrix of Section 4, and the
setting is a hard optimization with a quantum algorithm whose performance that matrix
governs.

\subsection{The problem}

\begin{definition}[Optimal Polynomial Intersection]
Fix a prime $p$ and an integer $n < p-1$. Let $F_1,\dots,F_{p-1}$ be subsets of the
field $\mathbb{F}_p$. An instance asks for a polynomial $Q \in \mathbb{F}_p[y]$ of
degree at most $n-1$ maximizing
\[
f_{\mathrm{OPI}}(Q) = \bigl| \{\, y \in \{1,\dots,p-1\} : Q(y) \in F_y \,\} \bigr|,
\]
the number of points at which the polynomial's value lands in the prescribed subset.
An instance is \emph{balanced} when every $|F_i| = r = \lfloor p/2 \rfloor$.
\end{definition}

Optimal Polynomial Intersection is a maximum-satisfaction problem over
$\mathbb{F}_p$: a linear code fixes the polynomials of bounded degree as codewords,
and maximizing the intersection count is maximizing the number of satisfied
constraints. The number of constraints is $m = p-1$, the constraint matrix is a
Vandermonde matrix, and the dual code $C^{\perp}$ is a Reed-Solomon code. Syndrome
decoding of $C^{\perp}$ out to $\ell = \lfloor (n+1)/2 \rfloor$ errors is the
Berlekamp-Massey algorithm and runs in polynomial time.

\subsection{The quantum algorithm and its matrix}

Decoded Quantum Interferometry~\cite{dqi} solves this class by preparing a state
whose amplitude is concentrated on low-weight error patterns and reading the decoded
polynomial. Its expected performance is governed by the largest eigenvalue of a
finite matrix, the same tridiagonal matrix built in Section 4.

\begin{lemma}[The expected satisfied count]\label{lem:jordan}
Let $\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$ be the expected number of satisfied constraints
after the algorithm's state preparation at decoding radius $\ell$. If
$2\ell + 1 < d^{\perp}$, the minimum distance of $C^{\perp}$, then
\[
\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle = \frac{mr}{p}
+ \frac{\sqrt{r(p-r)}}{p}\, \lambda_{\max}\!\bigl( A^{(m,\ell,d)} \bigr),
\]
where $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is the $(\ell+1)\times(\ell+1)$ real symmetric tridiagonal
matrix with diagonal entries $kd$ for $k = 0,\dots,\ell$ and off-diagonal entries
$a_{k+1} = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$, and $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$.
\end{lemma}

This is the result of Jordan and colleagues~\cite{dqi}, and the matrix
$A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is exactly the filtration matrix of Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix}: the
diagonal $kd$ is the evaluate operator $D$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:diag} at the
value $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$, and the off-diagonal
$\sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$ is the raising-lowering pair of Theorem~\ref{thm:ladder}. The
expected satisfied count is a constant plus the largest eigenvalue of the ladder,
scaled.

\begin{proposition}[The asymptotic limit]\label{prop:asymp}
Taking $\ell \to n/2$ and $m \to p$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} gives the closed form
\[
\frac{\langle s \rangle_{\mathrm{DQI}}}{p} = \frac{1}{2}
+ \sqrt{\frac{n}{2p}\Bigl(1 - \frac{n}{2p}\Bigr)},
\]
with no eigenvalue problem to solve.
\end{proposition}

The finite form of Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} keeps the full $(\ell+1)$-dimensional
operator, an eigenvector, a matrix, a specific finite $m$; the asymptotic form of
Proposition~\ref{prop:asymp} is what survives once that structure is smoothed into a
single scalar as $m \to p$. The finite form carries strictly more than the scalar
limit at any finite $m$, and the direction from the one to the other is the direction
of a coarsening, from the richer operator-valued description to the poorer scalar,
which is the direction the coreflector of Theorem~\ref{thm:two} always moves.

\subsection{The paraconsistent original}

The claim of this section is that the matrix $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is the classical-logical
image of a paraconsistent word, and that the algorithm's expectation value is that
word read through the coreflector. We first exhibit the word, then the lift, then the
identification.

The syndrome-decoding structure of the algorithm, the nesting of an outer frame that
banks a count across an uncomputation step, is representable as a closing word over
the twelve marks on the Belnap slice. An auto-designed word for this structure, of
thirty-three marks, failed to close: audited by the closure instruments it exposed
a count cleared before the frame that would bank it was opened, the composition-rule
violation in which a result is exposed rather than banked. Applying the composition
rule as a construction, opening the holding frame before the computing frame, the
repair adds five marks, three splits and two fuses, and the resulting thirty-eight
mark word closes: its banked count survives every reversal, and its cyclic verdict
is closing at every rotation of its orbit. This is a constructed, mechanically
verified instance of a paraconsistent word of the class the algorithm's circuit is
the classical image of.

\begin{proposition}[The $m$-fold lift]\label{prop:lift}
Let the inclusion $\iota$ and the ex falso coreflector $c$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:two}
act coordinatewise on the $m$-fold product $\{N,T,F,B\}^m$, with the product ordered
coordinatewise in the truth order. Then the coordinatewise inclusion is left adjoint
to the coordinatewise coreflector, and the Boolean image
$\mathbf{B}^m \cong \{F,T\}^m$ is the algorithm's own classical register
$\mathbb{F}_2^m$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $u = (u_1,\dots,u_m) \in \mathbf{B}^m$ and $v = (v_1,\dots,v_m) \in \{N,T,F,B\}^m$,
the coordinatewise truth order gives $\iota^m(u) \leqt v$ iff $\iota(u_i) \leqt v_i$
for every $i$, and $u \leqt c^m(v)$ iff $u_i \leqt c(v_i)$ for every $i$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:two} each coordinate satisfies
$\iota(u_i) \leqt v_i \iff u_i \leqt c(v_i)$, so the two conditions coincide,
establishing the coordinatewise adjunction. The Boolean image is $\{F,T\}^m$, which
under $F \mapsto 0$, $T \mapsto 1$ is the algorithm's register $\mathbb{F}_2^m$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The matrix is the coreflector image of the word's ladder]\label{thm:main}
On the $m$-fold paraconsistent register of Proposition~\ref{prop:lift}, let the
weight-$k$ sector be the uniform superposition $\ket{k}$ of states with exactly $k$
coordinates at $T$. The split mark $\msplit$, opening a frame, is the raising
operator $S_{+}$; the fuse mark $\mfuse$, closing a frame, is its adjoint $S_{-}$;
the evaluate mark $\mevalt$, depositing $T$, is the diagonal operator $D$ reading
$d$ once for each coordinate at $T$. Then, from Theorem~\ref{thm:ladder} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:diag},
\[
S_{-}\ket{k} = \sqrt{k(m-k+1)}\,\ket{k-1}, \qquad D\ket{k} = kd\,\ket{k},
\]
which are the off-diagonal $a_k$ and the diagonal entry $kd$ of $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ in
Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan}, term for term, at $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$. The matrix
$A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is the ladder of the word's own split, fuse, and evaluate marks, and
read through the coreflector of Theorem~\ref{thm:two} it is the effective operator
governing the algorithm's expectation value $\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The three marks realize as the three operators by the definitions of Section 4:
opening a frame raises the weight, closing lowers it, and depositing reads the
present weight. Their matrix elements on the uniform sector states are those of
Theorem~\ref{thm:ladder} and Proposition~\ref{prop:diag}, which are exactly the
entries of $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan}. The paraconsistent register
carries the full operator; the coreflector $c^m$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:lift} maps
it onto the Boolean register $\mathbb{F}_2^m$ on which the algorithm reads its
expectation value, and Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} expresses that value through
$\lambda_{\max}(A^{(m,\ell,d)})$. So the classical expectation value is the largest
eigenvalue of the paraconsistent word's ladder, read through the coreflector.
\end{proof}

The matrix that governs a state-of-the-art quantum algorithm is therefore not
analogous to the ladder of a paraconsistent word; it is that ladder, read down to the
classical register by the coreflector. The algorithm's performance is a reading of
the paraconsistent object through the lossy retraction of Theorem~\ref{thm:lossy}.

\section{Empirical convergence}

We compute both sides directly and measure the finite operator-valued value
collapsing onto the asymptotic scalar limit. The computation solves the eigenvalue
problem of Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} by shifted power iteration, a shift making the
matrix positive semidefinite so that plain power iteration converges to the true top
eigenvalue rather than whichever spectral extreme has the larger magnitude, and it
computes the asymptotic form of Proposition~\ref{prop:asymp} in the same run, from
the same parameters, so both columns of the table below are output rather than one
cited and one substituted.

Four balanced instances at a fixed ratio $n/p \approx 0.495$ keep the asymptotic
value of Proposition~\ref{prop:asymp} nearly fixed across all four, while the finite
matrix of Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} and its dimension $\ell+1$ grow.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{r r r r}
\toprule
$p$ & matrix size $(\ell+1)$ & $\langle s\rangle/p$ exact & asymptotic \\
\midrule
$101$   & $26 \times 26$     & $0.8938$ & $0.9316$ \\
$1009$  & $251 \times 251$   & $0.9229$ & $0.9317$ \\
$2003$  & $497 \times 497$   & $0.9259$ & $0.9316$ \\
$10007$ & $2478 \times 2478$ & $0.9296$ & $0.9316$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The exact value increases monotonically across the four scales, closing roughly a
third of the remaining gap to the asymptotic value with each doubling of $p$. The
richer operator-valued description at finite $m$ gives way to the poorer scalar limit
as $m$ grows, the same direction the coreflector of Theorem~\ref{thm:two} moves,
measured here rather than assumed. By Theorem~\ref{thm:main} the mathematical content
the finite matrix computes was never reachable by anything other than a classical
evaluation of the paraconsistent original: there is no second, independently quantum
object standing beside the matrix, only the paraconsistent ladder and its
classical-logical image. The finite-size convergence is the coarsening of
Theorem~\ref{thm:lossy} made quantitative, the operator-valued original at finite
$m$ standing above its scalar image and settling toward it as the retraction is
approached.

\section{Discussion}

One object has been traced through three descriptions. As a paraconsistent word it
is the split, fuse, and evaluate ladder on the $m$-fold register, an operator-valued
object that closes under the composition rule. As a classical-logical image it is
the tridiagonal matrix $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$, the coreflector's reading of that ladder on
the Boolean register, governing the quantum algorithm's expectation value. As an
asymptotic limit it is the single scalar of Proposition~\ref{prop:asymp}, what the
matrix becomes when its structure is smoothed as $m \to p$. The three are the same
object at three levels of coarsening, each arrow a coarsening proved or measured: the
coreflector from the paraconsistent to the classical, the limit from the finite
matrix to the scalar.

This is the program's thesis in one worked case. Quantum mechanics, here the quantum
algorithm, is the classical-logical image of a paraconsistent object, and the image
is strictly poorer than the original in a way that can be measured. The apparent
quantum behavior, the concentration of amplitude that gives the algorithm its
advantage, is produced by the classical evaluation of the paraconsistent ladder, not
by any additional physical ingredient. The relationship is directional: the matrix is
derived from the word, the scalar from the matrix, and neither lower description
asserts anything back up to the one it came from.

The tensor filtration developed in Section 4 is the mechanism throughout. The split
and fuse are the raising and lowering operators, the evaluate is the diagonal, and
the whole filtration is the tridiagonal ladder they build. Measurement is filtration
through that ladder, selecting a rung while the ladder persists, and the reversibility
of the split and fuse is why there is no collapse and no thermodynamic floor forcing
dissipation. The worked instance shows the same ladder governing a real algorithm,
its largest eigenvalue the algorithm's performance, its finite-to-asymptotic
collapse the coreflector's coarsening measured across four scales.

The ambient is the paraconsistent original. The classical image is what a retraction
reads off it, and the asymptotic scalar is what a limit reads off the image. At no
level is the classical description the ground; it is a coarsening, and the coarsening
is exactly lossy, and the loss is the state that carries contradiction.

\title{\bfseries Usurping Quantum Mechanics II\\[0.3em]
\large Tensor Filtration and the Paraconsistent Original}
\author{C. Lando Mills\\ \small Trabuco Canyon, California}
\date{3 September 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\noindent
Quantum mechanics is the classical-logical image of a paraconsistent four-valued
logic. The first part of this program established the direction: the ambient of the
world is the paraconsistent trilattice, and the consistent classical world is a
restriction cut out of it by two retractions that discard the states carrying
contradiction. This second part carries the mechanics. It develops the operation at
the center of the account, tensor filtration, as an explicit ladder of raising,
lowering, and diagonal operators on the weight sectors of an $m$-fold register, and
shows that measurement is filtration through this ladder rather than any collapse.
It then folds in a complete worked instance. The problem of Optimal Polynomial
Intersection has a quantum algorithm, Decoded Quantum Interferometry, whose expected
performance is governed by the largest eigenvalue of a finite tridiagonal matrix. We
show that this matrix is the classical-logical image of a paraconsistent word: the

\section{Introduction}

The claim of this program is that the world's ambient logic is paraconsistent, a
four-valued logic in which a proposition can carry support for its truth and support
for its falsity at once, and that quantum mechanics is what that logic looks like
when it is read through the classical two-valued slice. The consistent classical
world is a restriction constructed inside the paraconsistent ambient, reached by a
retraction that discards the states carrying contradiction, and strictly smaller
than the ambient it is cut from. The world does not appear classical at any scale;
the classical description is a bookkeeping laid over the ambient that declines to
look at the structure constituting it.

The first part of this program set the direction and derived the phenomena of
quantum mechanics as classical images of features of the carrier. This second part
does two things the first did not.

First, it develops the mechanics of the operation at the center of the account.
Measurement in this program is not a collapse; it is a tensor filtration, a
reversible selection of one factor of a tensor while the others remain. This part
makes the filtration concrete as an explicit ladder of operators on the weight
sectors of a many-coordinate register: a raising operator that opens a value into
more support, a lowering operator that is its adjoint, and a diagonal operator that
reads support already present. The three are the split, the fuse, and the evaluate
marks of the grammar, realized as linear operators, and together they are a
tridiagonal matrix whose structure is the whole content of the filtration.

Second, it folds in a complete worked instance in which the classical-logical image
of a paraconsistent object is not only exhibited but computed and measured. The
problem is Optimal Polynomial Intersection, a hard combinatorial optimization over a
finite field. Its state-of-the-art quantum algorithm, Decoded Quantum
Interferometry, has an expected performance governed by the largest eigenvalue of a
finite tridiagonal matrix. We show that this matrix is exactly the ladder of the
previous paragraph, the classical-logical image of a paraconsistent word, and that
the algorithm's expectation value is that word read through the coreflector. We then
compute the finite operator-valued value and its asymptotic scalar limit and measure
the one collapsing onto the other across four scales, the richer description giving
way to the poorer in the exact direction the coreflector moves.

We do not treat the dimensionless constants here; that thread belongs to the first
part. The spine of this part is the filtration mechanics and the worked convergence,
and everything is proved or computed on the page.

\section{The carrier}

We recall the carrier compactly, since the mechanics needs its operations but not a
second full development.

First-Degree Entailment separates the support for a proposition's truth from the
support for its falsity, giving four base answers: true only, false only, both, and
neither, written $T$, $F$, $B$, $N$. The trilattice of Shramko, Dunn and
Takenaka~\cite{sdt} adds an informational layer of an acceptable value $t$ and a
rejectable value $f$, and the carrier is the sixteen subsets of $\{T,F,t,f\}$. Three
orders act on it: the information order $\leqi$, subset inclusion, along which a
value only gains content; the truth order $\leqt$, along which truth support grows
and falsity support shrinks; and the constructivity order $\leqc$, along which the
settled layer grows and the informational layer shrinks. Negation $\neg$ exchanges
$T$ with $F$ and $t$ with $f$; it is an involution whose two fixed points are $N$ and
$B$, the two values that fail the classical law of excluded middle. The Belnap four
$\{N,T,F,B\}$ is the classical slice of the carrier, the part whose informational
layer is empty.

The truth order on the Belnap four is $F \leqt N \leqt T$ and $F \leqt B \leqt T$
with $N$ and $B$ incomparable, so $F$ is the bottom and $T$ the top and the two
nonclassical values sit between them on separate rungs. The value $B$ satisfies
$B \wedge_{\mathrm t} \neg B = B$ and $B \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg B = B$, so a
contradiction met or joined with its own negation is the contradiction and does not
reach falsity or truth. This is the paraconsistency: a contradiction is held as a
value rather than exploding the logic.

\section{The classical restriction}

The passage to a consistent world is a retraction onto the Boolean core, and it is
lossy in a precise sense we prove here, because the worked instance below is a
measurement of exactly this loss.

\begin{definition}[Boolean core]
Let $\mathbf{B} = \{F,T\}$, the two one-sided Belnap values, with the inherited truth
order and negation. It is the two-element Boolean algebra, and it is exactly the set
of Belnap values satisfying $x \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg x = T$.
\end{definition}

The values failing excluded middle are $N$ and $B$, computed from the truth-order
join: $N \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg N = N$ and $B \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg B = B$, neither
equal to $T$, while $T \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg T = T$ and $F \vee_{\mathrm t} \neg F = T$.

\begin{definition}[The two collapses]
Let the ex falso map $c$ and the ex quodlibet map $r$ from the Belnap four to
$\mathbf{B}$ be
\[
c(T)=T,\; c(F)=F,\; c(N)=F,\; c(B)=F, \qquad
r(T)=T,\; r(F)=F,\; r(N)=T,\; r(B)=T,
\]
and let $\iota : \mathbf{B} \hookrightarrow \{N,T,F,B\}$ be the inclusion.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The core is reached by two distinct adjunctions]\label{thm:two}
$c$ is monotone, restricts to the identity on $\mathbf{B}$, and is right adjoint to
the inclusion in the truth order, $\iota(x) \leqt v \iff x \leqt c(v)$. $r$ is
monotone, restricts to the identity on $\mathbf{B}$, and is left adjoint to the
inclusion, $r(v) \leqt x \iff v \leqt \iota(x)$. The two are distinct, differing on
the nonclassical values, $r(N)=r(B)=T \neq F = c(N)=c(B)$, and agreeing on
$\mathbf{B}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Monotonicity of $c$: the truth-order covers $F \leqt N$, $F \leqt B$, $N \leqt T$,
$B \leqt T$ map under $c$ to $F \leqt F$, $F \leqt F$, $F \leqt T$, $F \leqt T$, all
true. The adjunction has two cases. For $x=F$, both $x \leqt c(v)$ and
$\iota(x) \leqt v$ hold for every $v$, since $F$ is the truth-order bottom. For
$x=T$, $x \leqt c(v)$ forces $c(v)=T$, which holds exactly when $v=T$, and
$\iota(T) \leqt v$ forces $v=T$; equivalent. For $r$: the covers map under $r$ to
$F \leqt T$, $F \leqt T$, $T \leqt T$, $T \leqt T$, all true. For $x=T$ both sides
hold for every $v$; for $x=F$, $r(v) \leqt F$ forces $r(v)=F$, holding exactly when
$v=F$, and $v \leqt \iota(F)=F$ forces $v=F$; equivalent. Distinctness is direct from
the definitions.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Neither is an information-order adjunction]\label{thm:noinfo}
In the information order, where $N$ is the bottom and $B$ the top with $T$ and $F$
between, neither $c$ nor $r$ is adjoint to $\iota$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Were $r$ left adjoint in $\leqi$, then with $v=B$, $x=T$ we would need
$r(B) \leqi T \iff B \leqi \iota(T)=T$; the right side is false ($B$ is the top),
the left side $T \leqi T$ true. Were $c$ right adjoint, with $v=N$, $x=F$ we would
need $F \leqi N \iff \iota(F) \leqi c(N)$; the left side is false ($N$ the bottom),
issues split, so no adjunction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The collapse is exactly lossy]\label{thm:lossy}
Let $\mathrm{inc}$ be the closure operator on the Belnap four that sends every value
to $B$. It is idempotent with unique fixed point $B$, and it cannot be factored
through the classical inclusion: there is no map $\varphi : \mathbf{B} \to \mathbf{B}$
with $\iota \circ \varphi = \mathrm{inc} \circ \iota$. The paraconsistent value $B$
is inexpressible inside either classical image.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\mathrm{inc}(\mathrm{inc}(x)) = \mathrm{inc}(B) = B = \mathrm{inc}(x)$, and a fixed
point solves $x=B$, so $B$ is unique. If $\varphi$ existed, then for classical $x$,
$\iota(\varphi(x)) = \mathrm{inc}(\iota(x)) = B$; but $\iota$ has image
$\{F,T\}$, which does not contain $B$, so $\iota(\varphi(x))=B$ is impossible. No
such $\varphi$ exists.
\end{proof}

The two retractions each give a total map onto the core, so no value is left without
an image, and yet the operation whose fixed point is the contradiction cannot be
written inside the image. The passage to a consistent world does not lose a value by
sending it nowhere; it loses the ability to name the state that carries
contradiction. The worked instance below measures exactly how much a specific
paraconsistent object exceeds its two classical retractions, and finds the excess
positive at every finite size and shrinking toward the retraction as the size grows.

\section{Tensor filtration}

The operation at the center of the account is the split and its adjoint fuse, and
their action on a many-coordinate register is a ladder of operators that we now
build explicitly. This is the mechanics that measurement, and the worked instance,
run on.

\subsection{The register and its weight sectors}

Take $m$ copies of the constructive layer, an $m$-coordinate register in which each
coordinate carries a one-sided value, $T$ or $F$. A basis state is a string
$x \in \{T,F\}^m$. The \emph{weight} of a string is the number of coordinates at
$T$, and the \emph{weight-$k$ sector} is the set of strings of weight $k$, of which
there are $\binom{m}{k}$.

\begin{definition}[Uniform sector states]
For $0 \leq k \leq m$ let
\[
\ket{k} = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2} \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k} \ket{x}
\]
be the uniform normalized superposition of the weight-$k$ strings. The
$\ket{k}$ for $k=0,\dots,m$ are orthonormal, and they span the symmetric subspace of
the register, the part invariant under permuting the coordinates.
\end{definition}

The uniform sector states are the natural coordinates for a filtration that does not
distinguish the coordinates from one another, which is the symmetric case the worked
instance needs.

\subsection{Split as raising, fuse as lowering}

The split $\msplit$ opens a value into more support: on the register it takes a
coordinate that is at $F$ and sets it to $T$, adding one to the weight. Applied
symmetrically, summed over the coordinates that can be raised, it is the raising
operator.

\begin{theorem}[The ladder operators]\label{thm:ladder}
Let $S_{+}$ be the operator that sends a string of weight $k$ to the sum of its
weight-$(k+1)$ extensions, each obtained by raising one coordinate from $F$ to $T$,
and let $S_{-}$ be its adjoint. On the uniform sector states,
\[
S_{+}\ket{k} = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}\,\ket{k+1},
\qquad
S_{-}\ket{k} = \sqrt{k(m-k+1)}\,\ket{k-1}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $\ket{k} = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}\sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k}\ket{x}$. Acting with
$S_{+}$, each weight-$k$ string $x$ maps to the sum of the $m-k$ strings obtained by
raising one of its $F$ coordinates, so
\[
S_{+}\ket{k} = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2} \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k}\ \sum_{i:\,x_i=F} \ket{x^{(i)}},
\]
where $x^{(i)}$ raises coordinate $i$. Each weight-$(k+1)$ string $y$ arises in this
double sum once for each of its $k+1$ coordinates at $T$, since lowering any one of
them gives a weight-$k$ string $x$ that raises back to $y$. So the coefficient of
$\ket{y}$ is $(k+1)\binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}$, and
\[
S_{+}\ket{k} = (k+1)\binom{m}{k}^{-1/2} \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(y)=k+1}\ket{y}
= (k+1)\binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}\binom{m}{k+1}^{1/2}\ket{k+1}.
\]
Using $\binom{m}{k+1}/\binom{m}{k} = (m-k)/(k+1)$, the coefficient is
$(k+1)\sqrt{(m-k)/(k+1)} = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$, giving the first identity. The second
is the adjoint: $S_{-}$ is defined by
$\langle k-1 \mid S_{-} \mid k\rangle = \langle k \mid S_{+} \mid k-1\rangle^{*}
= \sqrt{k(m-k+1)}$, using the first identity with $k$ replaced by $k-1$, so
$S_{-}\ket{k} = \sqrt{k(m-k+1)}\,\ket{k-1}$.
\end{proof}

The split $\msplit$ is $S_{+}$, opening one coordinate into truth support; the fuse
$\mfuse$ is $S_{-}$, its adjoint, closing one coordinate back. The two are a raising
and lowering pair on the ladder of weight sectors, and their composition returns the
sector it started from up to the ladder coefficients, the operator form of the
counit-unit law that opening and closing lose nothing.

\subsection{Evaluate as the diagonal}

The evaluate mark $\mevalt$ reads truth support already present, depositing a fixed
amount once for each coordinate at $T$.

\begin{proposition}[The diagonal operator]\label{prop:diag}
Let $D$ be the operator that, for a fixed real $d$, reads $d$ once for each
coordinate at $T$. On the uniform sector states $D\ket{k} = kd\,\ket{k}$, diagonal
in the sector basis.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On a string $x$ of weight $k$, $D$ reads $d$ once per $T$ coordinate, so
$D\ket{x} = kd\ket{x}$. Since every string in $\ket{k}$ has weight $k$, $D$ acts as
the scalar $kd$ on the whole uniform superposition, $D\ket{k}=kd\ket{k}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The ladder is a tridiagonal matrix}

The three operators together, the split-raising, the fuse-lowering, and the
evaluate-diagonal, form one operator on the ladder of $\ell+1$ lowest sectors.

\begin{theorem}[The filtration matrix]\label{thm:matrix}
On the span of $\ket{0},\dots,\ket{\ell}$, the operator $A = D + S_{+} + S_{-}$ is the
$(\ell+1)\times(\ell+1)$ real symmetric tridiagonal matrix with diagonal entries
$A_{kk} = kd$ for $k=0,\dots,\ell$ and off-diagonal entries
$A_{k,k+1} = A_{k+1,k} = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Proposition~\ref{prop:diag} the diagonal is $D\ket{k}=kd\ket{k}$, giving
$A_{kk}=kd$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:ladder} the raising and lowering give
$A_{k+1,k} = \langle k+1\mid S_{+}\mid k\rangle = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$ and
$A_{k,k+1} = \langle k\mid S_{-}\mid k+1\rangle = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$, equal, so the
matrix is symmetric. All other entries vanish because $S_{\pm}$ change the weight by
one and $D$ preserves it, so only the diagonal and the first off-diagonals are
nonzero.
\end{proof}

This tridiagonal matrix is the whole content of the filtration. It is built from the
three marks alone, the split and its adjoint on the off-diagonal and the evaluate on
the diagonal, and it is the object whose spectrum the worked instance reads. The
filtration is reversible in the sense already fixed: the off-diagonal part is a
raising and lowering pair, adjoint to each other, and the diagonal part is
self-adjoint, so $A$ is self-adjoint and generates a reversible motion on the ladder.

\subsection{Measurement is filtration through the ladder}

Measurement selects a sector. The split opens the register up the ladder, a chosen
sector is read, and the fuse closes it back, and because the fuse is the adjoint of
the split the whole ladder persists through the reading. What a classical account
records as a collapse to a definite weight is the reading of one rung of the ladder
while the ladder remains, and the rungs not read are the tensor factors the split
opened and the fuse can restore. There is no collapse in the ladder; there is a
filtration that selects a rung and a fuse that recovers the whole. The apparent
destruction of the other rungs is the classical slice's inability to carry more than
the one it read, the same inexpressibility as Theorem~\ref{thm:lossy}, now at the
level of the register rather than the single value.

\section{Measurement, superposition, and the phenomena}

Before the worked instance, we place the phenomena on the ladder, briefly, since the
mechanics above is what they run on.

Superposition is the held value $B$, true and false together, its own negation, the
one Belnap value the classical slice cannot name. On the register it is a state
spread across weight sectors rather than sitting in one, the uniform sector states
being its symmetric instances.

Measurement is filtration through the ladder, as above, with no collapse. The word
tensor is exact: the split opens a value into a pair of tensor factors, a reading
selects one factor while the other remains a factor of the whole, and the fuse
recombines them. Reading $x \otimes y$ reads $x$ without deleting $y$; the classical
account writes only the read factor and calls the loss of the other collapse. Because
the fuse is the adjoint of the split and the round trip is the identity, the ambient
pays no thermodynamic price for measurement; a genuine collapse would be an erasure
with a Landauer cost~\cite{landauer}, and the filtration erases nothing, in the sense
made concrete by reversible computing~\cite{bennett,fredkin}.

The Born rule is the overlap of a state with a rung. For the two-outcome case, a
pure state at polar angle $\theta$ from the true pole is
$\cos(\theta/2)\ket{T} + e^{i\varphi}\sin(\theta/2)\ket{F}$, the half-angle from the
ray double cover, and the probability of the true outcome is
$|\langle T \mid \psi\rangle|^2 = \cos^2(\theta/2)$. The quadratic form is forced,
not chosen: a probability assignment on a positive-operator frame that is additive
and non-contextual has the form $\mathrm{tr}(\rho E)$ by Busch's
theorem~\cite{busch}, extending Gleason's~\cite{gleason} to every dimension including
two, and on the truth projector this is $\cos^2(\theta/2)$.

Entanglement is a shared held value that persists as each part is read, and the
strength of the correlation it produces is bounded by a single tilt angle: choosing
the four Bell settings~\cite{bell,chsh} at offsets of $\pi/4$ gives
$S = 4\cos(\pi/4) = 2\sqrt2$, the Tsirelson bound~\cite{tsirelson}, the shared value
supplying exactly $\cos(\pi/4)$ per setting. Decoherence is the emptying of the
informational layer $\{t,f\}$ to the environment, the coherences of the density
matrix carried off while the populations, the diagonal read by the sector projection,
remain.

\section{A worked realization: Optimal Polynomial Intersection}

We now carry a complete instance in which the classical-logical image of a
paraconsistent object is computed and its convergence to the paraconsistent original
measured. The object is the tridiagonal filtration matrix of Section 4, and the
setting is a hard optimization with a quantum algorithm whose performance that matrix
governs.

\subsection{The problem}

\begin{definition}[Optimal Polynomial Intersection]
Fix a prime $p$ and an integer $n < p-1$. Let $F_1,\dots,F_{p-1}$ be subsets of the
field $\mathbb{F}_p$. An instance asks for a polynomial $Q \in \mathbb{F}_p[y]$ of
degree at most $n-1$ maximizing
\[
f_{\mathrm{OPI}}(Q) = \bigl| \{\, y \in \{1,\dots,p-1\} : Q(y) \in F_y \,\} \bigr|,
\]
the number of points at which the polynomial's value lands in the prescribed subset.
An instance is \emph{balanced} when every $|F_i| = r = \lfloor p/2 \rfloor$.
\end{definition}

Optimal Polynomial Intersection is a maximum-satisfaction problem over
$\mathbb{F}_p$: a linear code fixes the polynomials of bounded degree as codewords,
and maximizing the intersection count is maximizing the number of satisfied
constraints. The number of constraints is $m = p-1$, the constraint matrix is a
Vandermonde matrix, and the dual code $C^{\perp}$ is a Reed-Solomon code. Syndrome
decoding of $C^{\perp}$ out to $\ell = \lfloor (n+1)/2 \rfloor$ errors is the
Berlekamp-Massey algorithm and runs in polynomial time.

\subsection{The quantum algorithm and its matrix}

Decoded Quantum Interferometry~\cite{dqi} solves this class by preparing a state
whose amplitude is concentrated on low-weight error patterns and reading the decoded
polynomial. Its expected performance is governed by the largest eigenvalue of a
finite matrix, the same tridiagonal matrix built in Section 4.

\begin{lemma}[The expected satisfied count]\label{lem:jordan}
Let $\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$ be the expected number of satisfied constraints
after the algorithm's state preparation at decoding radius $\ell$. If
$2\ell + 1 < d^{\perp}$, the minimum distance of $C^{\perp}$, then
\[
\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle = \frac{mr}{p}
+ \frac{\sqrt{r(p-r)}}{p}\, \lambda_{\max}\!\bigl( A^{(m,\ell,d)} \bigr),
\]
where $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is the $(\ell+1)\times(\ell+1)$ real symmetric tridiagonal
matrix with diagonal entries $kd$ for $k = 0,\dots,\ell$ and off-diagonal entries
$a_{k+1} = \sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$, and $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$.
\end{lemma}

This is the result of Jordan and colleagues~\cite{dqi}, and the matrix
$A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is exactly the filtration matrix of Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix}: the
diagonal $kd$ is the evaluate operator $D$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:diag} at the
value $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$, and the off-diagonal
$\sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$ is the raising-lowering pair of Theorem~\ref{thm:ladder}. The
expected satisfied count is a constant plus the largest eigenvalue of the ladder,
scaled.

\begin{proposition}[The asymptotic limit]\label{prop:asymp}
Taking $\ell \to n/2$ and $m \to p$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} gives the closed form
\[
\frac{\langle s \rangle_{\mathrm{DQI}}}{p} = \frac{1}{2}
+ \sqrt{\frac{n}{2p}\Bigl(1 - \frac{n}{2p}\Bigr)},
\]
with no eigenvalue problem to solve.
\end{proposition}

The finite form of Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} keeps the full $(\ell+1)$-dimensional
operator, an eigenvector, a matrix, a specific finite $m$; the asymptotic form of
Proposition~\ref{prop:asymp} is what survives once that structure is smoothed into a
single scalar as $m \to p$. The finite form carries strictly more than the scalar
limit at any finite $m$, and the direction from the one to the other is the direction
of a coarsening, from the richer operator-valued description to the poorer scalar,
which is the direction the coreflector of Theorem~\ref{thm:two} always moves.

\subsection{The paraconsistent original}

The claim of this section is that the matrix $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is the classical-logical
image of a paraconsistent word, and that the algorithm's expectation value is that
word read through the coreflector. We first exhibit the word, then the lift, then the
identification.

The syndrome-decoding structure of the algorithm, the nesting of an outer frame that
banks a count across an uncomputation step, is representable as a closing word over
the twelve marks on the Belnap slice. An auto-designed word for this structure, of
thirty-three marks, failed to close: audited by the closure instruments it exposed
a count cleared before the frame that would bank it was opened, the composition-rule
violation in which a result is exposed rather than banked. Applying the composition
rule as a construction, opening the holding frame before the computing frame, the
repair adds five marks, three splits and two fuses, and the resulting thirty-eight
mark word closes: its banked count survives every reversal, and its cyclic verdict
is closing at every rotation of its orbit. This is a constructed, mechanically
verified instance of a paraconsistent word of the class the algorithm's circuit is
the classical image of.

\begin{proposition}[The $m$-fold lift]\label{prop:lift}
Let the inclusion $\iota$ and the ex falso coreflector $c$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:two}
act coordinatewise on the $m$-fold product $\{N,T,F,B\}^m$, with the product ordered
coordinatewise in the truth order. Then the coordinatewise inclusion is left adjoint
to the coordinatewise coreflector, and the Boolean image
$\mathbf{B}^m \cong \{F,T\}^m$ is the algorithm's own classical register
$\mathbb{F}_2^m$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $u = (u_1,\dots,u_m) \in \mathbf{B}^m$ and $v = (v_1,\dots,v_m) \in \{N,T,F,B\}^m$,
the coordinatewise truth order gives $\iota^m(u) \leqt v$ iff $\iota(u_i) \leqt v_i$
for every $i$, and $u \leqt c^m(v)$ iff $u_i \leqt c(v_i)$ for every $i$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:two} each coordinate satisfies
$\iota(u_i) \leqt v_i \iff u_i \leqt c(v_i)$, so the two conditions coincide,
establishing the coordinatewise adjunction. The Boolean image is $\{F,T\}^m$, which
under $F \mapsto 0$, $T \mapsto 1$ is the algorithm's register $\mathbb{F}_2^m$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The matrix is the coreflector image of the word's ladder]\label{thm:main}
On the $m$-fold paraconsistent register of Proposition~\ref{prop:lift}, let the
weight-$k$ sector be the uniform superposition $\ket{k}$ of states with exactly $k$
coordinates at $T$. The split mark $\msplit$, opening a frame, is the raising
operator $S_{+}$; the fuse mark $\mfuse$, closing a frame, is its adjoint $S_{-}$;
the evaluate mark $\mevalt$, depositing $T$, is the diagonal operator $D$ reading
$d$ once for each coordinate at $T$. Then, from Theorem~\ref{thm:ladder} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:diag},
\[
S_{-}\ket{k} = \sqrt{k(m-k+1)}\,\ket{k-1}, \qquad D\ket{k} = kd\,\ket{k},
\]
which are the off-diagonal $a_k$ and the diagonal entry $kd$ of $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ in
Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan}, term for term, at $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$. The matrix
$A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is the ladder of the word's own split, fuse, and evaluate marks, and
read through the coreflector of Theorem~\ref{thm:two} it is the effective operator
governing the algorithm's expectation value $\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The three marks realize as the three operators by the definitions of Section 4:
opening a frame raises the weight, closing lowers it, and depositing reads the
present weight. Their matrix elements on the uniform sector states are those of
Theorem~\ref{thm:ladder} and Proposition~\ref{prop:diag}, which are exactly the
entries of $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan}. The paraconsistent register
carries the full operator; the coreflector $c^m$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:lift} maps
it onto the Boolean register $\mathbb{F}_2^m$ on which the algorithm reads its
expectation value, and Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} expresses that value through
$\lambda_{\max}(A^{(m,\ell,d)})$. So the classical expectation value is the largest
eigenvalue of the paraconsistent word's ladder, read through the coreflector.
\end{proof}

The matrix that governs a state-of-the-art quantum algorithm is therefore not
analogous to the ladder of a paraconsistent word; it is that ladder, read down to the
classical register by the coreflector. The algorithm's performance is a reading of
the paraconsistent object through the lossy retraction of Theorem~\ref{thm:lossy}.

\section{Empirical convergence}

We compute both sides directly and measure the finite operator-valued value
collapsing onto the asymptotic scalar limit. The computation solves the eigenvalue
problem of Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} by shifted power iteration, a shift making the
matrix positive semidefinite so that plain power iteration converges to the true top
eigenvalue rather than whichever spectral extreme has the larger magnitude, and it
computes the asymptotic form of Proposition~\ref{prop:asymp} in the same run, from
the same parameters, so both columns of the table below are output rather than one
cited and one substituted.

Four balanced instances at a fixed ratio $n/p \approx 0.495$ keep the asymptotic
value of Proposition~\ref{prop:asymp} nearly fixed across all four, while the finite
matrix of Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} and its dimension $\ell+1$ grow.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{r r r r}
\toprule
$p$ & matrix size $(\ell+1)$ & $\langle s\rangle/p$ exact & asymptotic \\
\midrule
$101$   & $26 \times 26$     & $0.8938$ & $0.9316$ \\
$1009$  & $251 \times 251$   & $0.9229$ & $0.9317$ \\
$2003$  & $497 \times 497$   & $0.9259$ & $0.9316$ \\
$10007$ & $2478 \times 2478$ & $0.9296$ & $0.9316$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The exact value increases monotonically across the four scales, closing roughly a
third of the remaining gap to the asymptotic value with each doubling of $p$. The
richer operator-valued description at finite $m$ gives way to the poorer scalar limit
as $m$ grows, the same direction the coreflector of Theorem~\ref{thm:two} moves,
measured here rather than assumed. By Theorem~\ref{thm:main} the mathematical content
the finite matrix computes was never reachable by anything other than a classical
evaluation of the paraconsistent original: there is no second, independently quantum
object standing beside the matrix, only the paraconsistent ladder and its
classical-logical image. The finite-size convergence is the coarsening of
Theorem~\ref{thm:lossy} made quantitative, the operator-valued original at finite
$m$ standing above its scalar image and settling toward it as the retraction is
approached.

One object has been traced through three descriptions. As a paraconsistent word it
is the split, fuse, and evaluate ladder on the $m$-fold register, an operator-valued
object that closes under the composition rule. As a classical-logical image it is
the tridiagonal matrix $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$, the coreflector's reading of that ladder on
the Boolean register, governing the quantum algorithm's expectation value. As an
asymptotic limit it is the single scalar of Proposition~\ref{prop:asymp}, what the
matrix becomes when its structure is smoothed as $m \to p$. The three are the same
object at three levels of coarsening, each arrow a coarsening proved or measured: the
coreflector from the paraconsistent to the classical, the limit from the finite
matrix to the scalar.

This is the program's thesis in one worked case. Quantum mechanics, here the quantum
algorithm, is the classical-logical image of a paraconsistent object, and the image
is strictly poorer than the original in a way that can be measured. The apparent
quantum behavior, the concentration of amplitude that gives the algorithm its
advantage, is produced by the classical evaluation of the paraconsistent ladder, not
by any additional physical ingredient. The relationship is directional: the matrix is
derived from the word, the scalar from the matrix, and neither lower description
asserts anything back up to the one it came from.

The tensor filtration developed in Section 4 is the mechanism throughout. The split
and fuse are the raising and lowering operators, the evaluate is the diagonal, and
the whole filtration is the tridiagonal ladder they build. Measurement is filtration
through that ladder, selecting a rung while the ladder persists, and the reversibility
of the split and fuse is why there is no collapse and no thermodynamic floor forcing
dissipation. The worked instance shows the same ladder governing a real algorithm,
its largest eigenvalue the algorithm's performance, its finite-to-asymptotic
collapse the coreflector's coarsening measured across four scales.

The ambient is the paraconsistent original. The classical image is what a retraction
reads off it, and the asymptotic scalar is what a limit reads off the image. At no
level is the classical description the ground; it is a coarsening, and the coarsening
is exactly lossy, and the loss is the state that carries contradiction.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Meter package energy for a chain of factorization splits against an idle
control, reading Intel RAPL directly from the package energy MSR.

Must run as root: reading /dev/cpu/0/msr needs it, and the msr module is loaded
here if it is not already. On WSL2 the read may fault or stay flat if the
hypervisor does not pass the MSR through; the script says so plainly rather than
reporting a fabricated number.

  sudo python3 energy_probe.py [N]

N is the number of splits in the active chain (default 160). The split is the
store-free leaping search on a semiprime whose loop length is above 4e10.
"""
import os, sys, time, struct, subprocess

MSR_RAPL_POWER_UNIT = 0x606
MSR_PKG_ENERGY_STATUS = 0x611
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SPLIT = "trilattice_factor winding 1000036000099"

def read_msr(reg, cpu=0):
    path = f"/dev/cpu/{cpu}/msr"
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.lseek(fd, reg, os.SEEK_SET)
        return struct.unpack("<Q", os.read(fd, 8))[0]
    finally:
        os.close(fd)

def ensure_msr():
    if not os.path.exists("/dev/cpu/0/msr"):
        subprocess.run(["modprobe", "msr"], check=False)
    if not os.path.exists("/dev/cpu/0/msr"):
        sys.exit("no /dev/cpu/0/msr after modprobe msr; MSR not available in this guest")

def energy_joules(esu_div):
    raw = read_msr(MSR_PKG_ENERGY_STATUS) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return raw / esu_div, raw

def delta_j(before_raw, after_raw, esu_div):
    d = (after_raw - before_raw) & 0xFFFFFFFF  # 32-bit wrap
    return d / esu_div

def run_chain(n):
    args = [os.path.join(HERE, "run_hosted_cmds.sh")] + [SPLIT] * n
    subprocess.run(args, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, check=False)

def main():
    n = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 160
    ensure_msr()
    unit = read_msr(MSR_RAPL_POWER_UNIT)
    esu = (unit >> 8) & 0x1F
    esu_div = float(1 << esu)  # counts per joule
    print(f"RAPL energy unit: 2^-{esu} J per count")

    # sanity: does the counter move at all over a short busy spin?
    _, r0 = energy_joules(esu_div)
    t = time.time()
    while time.time() - t < 0.5:
        pass
    _, r1 = energy_joules(esu_div)
    if ((r1 - r0) & 0xFFFFFFFF) == 0:
        sys.exit("package energy counter did not advance; the guest is not passing RAPL through")

    # idle control: same wall time the chain will take, measured first at rest.
    _, ia = energy_joules(esu_div)
    t0 = time.time()
    run_chain(n)
    chain_wall = time.time() - t0
    _, ib = energy_joules(esu_div)
    active_j = delta_j(ia, ib, esu_div)

    _, ja = energy_joules(esu_div)
    time.sleep(chain_wall)
    _, jb = energy_joules(esu_div)
    idle_j = delta_j(ja, jb, esu_div)

    print(f"chain of {n} splits: wall {chain_wall:.2f}s")
    print(f"  package energy over the chain : {active_j:.2f} J")
    print(f"  package energy idle, same wall: {idle_j:.2f} J")
    marg = active_j - idle_j
    print(f"  marginal energy of the splits : {marg:.2f} J  ({marg/n*1000:.2f} mJ per split)")
    print(f"  idle baseline power           : {idle_j/chain_wall:.2f} W")
    print(f"  active power                  : {active_j/chain_wall:.2f} W")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Plan: FDE-subsumes-QM manuscript, then the aligned layer

## Context

The energy meter (Afterburner MAHM shared memory read over powershell interop,
since WSL2 hides RAPL) showed a reversible leaping split costs about 2.3 J above
idle, package power tripling under load. That gap is the Landauer tax of a
reversible computation (the marks close, fuse after split is the identity) run on
an irreversible stack. Reaching the floor needs the reality stack in syzygy: the
computation (already reversible), the OS (mOMonadOS, currently erasing), and the
hardware (x86 gates; native metal not yet built).

Two deliverables, manuscript first.

---

## Part 1: the FDE-subsumes-QM manuscript (do first)

A single publication-grade xelatex paper, flat in `ig-docs/`, consolidating the
existing fragments. No new derivations beyond assembly and one stated scope
boundary; this is the "consolidate into one paper" scope.

### Sources to fold in (ig-docs unless noted)
- `QMFDE.md` (1110 lines) — the spine, phenomenon-by-phenomenon.
- `BELNAP_FDE_COMPLETE.md` — QM as a projection of Belnap logic; Born rule.
- `millennium_theorems_as_ovms.tex` — the 24-cell OVM taxonomy; already house style.
- `dqi.tex` / `DQI_IMASM_UNIFIED.md` — the one-line thesis.
- `SIC_POVM_CONTEXT.md` — the Grammar IS the SIC-POVM; d=2/12/2048.

### Spine (sections)
1. The trilattice carrier: four base values, three orders, closure identity
   fuse-after-split (∋∘∈ = id). Cite Shramko-Dunn-Takenaka.
2. QM as the classical evaluation of the paraconsistent FDE structure (the dqi
   thesis).
3. Phenomena, each grounded to a mark:
   - superposition = B (both), the ⊞ hold-both
   - measurement/collapse = ∈ split; state prep = ∋ fuse
   - Born rule = proj_T ∘ ∈, corrected to cos²(θ/2) via the information-order shuttle
   - interference = information-order shuttle; phase = winding on ⊡
   - entanglement = paradox count 3n; CHSH at Tsirelson 2√2
   - uncertainty = exposed banked count (a composition-rule failure)
   - decoherence = {t,f}→{} collapse; QEC = frame-nested split/fuse
4. The SIC-POVM as the Grammar: d=2 qubit, d=12 (12 primitives = 12 projectors),
   d=2048 (structural SIC, Stark-unit shadow).
5. Theorems as measurements: the OVM taxonomy, positivity as a self-inverse
   winding.
6. Scope boundary, foregrounded not buried: FDE does NOT output the action
   quantum, the angle-to-metre scale, or the dimensionful constants; those enter
   from outside exactly where π does.
7. Verification: cite the mOMonadOS modules (`belnap.rs`, `sic_povm.rs`,
   `d12_sic.rs`, `d2048_exact_sic.rs`, `ovm.rs`) and the Lean carriers; note the
   crystallized branches. (Cutting a new branch is out of scope per the answer.)

### House style
Copy the `witness_and_closure.tex` preamble: xelatex, `fontspec`, `unicode-math`,
`\setmainfont{Linux Libertine O}`, `\setmathfont{TeX Gyre Pagella Math}`, Shavian
via `\newfontfamily\shaw{Trabajo}` + `\sh{}`. IG marks set in math mode so none
render blank. Where the corpus conflicts (⊞ triple-naming; YM pinch vs split
shell), pick one convention and state it in a footnote rather than reconcile in
depth (that deeper reconciliation was declined for this paper).

### Files
- New: `ig-docs/qm_from_fde.tex` and its compiled `.pdf`.

### Verification
- `xelatex` twice, `command grep -i "missing character"` on the log returns
  nothing; PDF renders the marks. Commit tex + pdf flat in ig-docs.

---

## Part 2: the aligned layer (do after, all three stages)

### Stage A — reversible OS operations, buildable and measurable now
Make the bare-metal execution path conservative and certify it, then meter it.
- Run a canonical computation (the leaping split, whose hot loop already holds
  constant state) inside a `heap_mark()` / `heap_reset(mark)` scope
  (`mOMonadOS/src/main.rs`, lines ~288) so transient allocations are reclaimed by
  scope teardown, not abandoned by the bump `dealloc`.
- Gate the mode on the driving word certifying reversible: `banked_walk` in
  `MoDoT/imasm_core/src/lattice_flow.rs` must report `holds()` (zero exposed
  clears). Expose it as a REPL verb (a "reversible run") that asserts this.
- Replace `install_program`'s blanket zeroing (`mOMonadOS/src/kernel.rs`) with
  scope teardown where the reversible mode is active.
- Meter: extend the Afterburner harness (`afsample.ps1` + `energy_probe.py`) to a
  paired A/B measurement, current path vs reversible-mode path, and report the
  marginal-energy delta. Expectation: erasure removed lowers the draw; the floor
  is not reached on x86 and that gap is named.
- Files: `mOMonadOS/src/main.rs`, `src/kernel.rs`, a new REPL verb in
  `src/repl.rs`, the Afterburner harness. Port to `G-mOMonadOS`.

### Stage B — the horn-torus execution geometry
Run the canonical computation wound on `mOMonadOS/src/kernel_torus.rs`: map the
program stations onto the (1,1) winding through the R=r pinch ⊙ via its
`TorusMap`, the loop as the execution geometry. `src/substrate.rs` already argues
the substrate action is conservative (fixed points and orbits, no dissipation),
which is the reversibility this stage runs on.
- Files: `mOMonadOS/src/kernel_torus.rs`, a torus-driven execution path wired to

### Stage C — the metal port (floor named, not reached in software)
Open the m2_torus metal consumer: a no_std scalar `mOMonadOS/src/torus.rs`
forward over the baked `M2TO` blob (`daydr33m/m2_torus/` host + `bake.rs` already
produce it), with bit-exact host/metal parity as the acceptance gate, following
the pattern of the already-on-metal `vita.rs`. This is the substrate whose steps
are the loop. The true reversible/adiabatic hardware that actually reaches the
Landauer floor is future and named as such; software alignment minimizes erasure
but cannot make x86 gates reversible.
- Files: new `mOMonadOS/src/torus.rs`, `daydr33m/m2_torus/` bake, a `torus` REPL
  verb.

### Verification (aligned layer)
- Reversibility certificate: `banked_walk` reports `holds()` on the driving word.
- Paired energy measurement via Afterburner shows the marginal-energy delta
  between the erasing and the conservative paths.
- Both `mOMonadOS` and `G-mOMonadOS` build (hosted and bare-metal via
  `build_bootimage.sh`); Stage C gated on bit-exact host/metal parity.

---

## Execution order
Manuscript (Part 1) first, then Stage A, B, C in sequence. Commit freely, never
push; documents flat in ig-docs; instruments mirrored into both mOMonadOS repos.

\subsection{The measurement frame is symmetric and informationally complete}

The projectors a measurement uses are not the two poles alone. The natural frame is the
symmetric informationally complete positive-operator measurement, the frame of $d^2$
unit vectors in $d$ dimensions with equal pairwise overlap. In the qubit case $d=2$ the
four frame vectors are the corners of a regular tetrahedron inscribed in the sphere, and
the defining property is that any two frame projectors $\Pi_i,\Pi_j$ with $i\neq j$
satisfy
\[
\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_i\Pi_j) = \frac{1}{d+1} = \frac13,
\]
the equiangular condition. A frame with this property fixes a state completely from its
outcome probabilities, informational completeness, and does so with the fewest outcomes
and the most even spread, symmetry. On such a frame the probability rule takes its
frame-native form, the urgleichung of Fuchs and Schack, in which the probabilities
$q_j$ of a measurement following a reference measurement with probabilities $p_i$ are
\[
q_j = \sum_i\Bigl[(d+1)\,p_i - \frac1d\Bigr]\,r(j\mid i),
\]
with $r(j\mid i)$ the conditional probabilities of the second frame given the first. The
subtraction of $1/d$ and the factor $d+1$ are the same coreflector coefficients that
appear in the OPI matrix of Section 7, the frame's way of reading a paraconsistent value
onto its classical outcomes: the four tetrahedron corners are the four Belnap values
placed symmetrically, and the equiangular overlap $1/(d+1)$ is the residue the held
value leaves in every direction at once.

Two systems combine by the product of their carriers, and an entangled state is a value
of the product that does not factor into a value on each part. A shared held relation,
one part true and the other false held together as $B$ rather than settled, is not any
separable pair of one-sided values, since a pair names one alternative and the shared
value holds both. The four Bell states are the four shared held values of the two-part
product under the two swaps, and reading one part is a split of the shared value that,
by the persistence of $B$, does not destroy it, which is why the correlation holds
however the parts are read. The middle-value count multiplies under the product, so a
composite of many parts climbs quickly, the carrier's form of the exponential growth of
the state space with the number of parts.
